course.title: CSS Mastery
course.subtitle: Complete CSS and Responsive Design Program
course.tagline: Style the Structure. Build Responsive Interfaces.
course.description: CSS from the first selector to Flexbox, Grid, responsive layout, animation, design tokens and a professional workflow. Twenty-four modules in five levels, ten learning sections each, with every sample written as a complete HTML document so the styled result is visible beside the code.
course.standard: CSS3 · Flexbox · Grid · Container Queries · Modern CSS
prerequisites: Basic HTML is recommended — every example includes the markup it styles
A browser and a plain text editor (VS Code recommended)
outcomes: Explain what CSS is and how the browser applies it to HTML
Write selectors that target exactly the elements you mean
Control colour, backgrounds, units and typography with confidence
Calculate an element's real size with the box model
Build layouts with Flexbox and Grid instead of guessing floats
Make a page work from phone to desktop with media and container queries
Style forms, buttons, cards and navigation accessibly
Use pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements, transitions and keyframes
Organise CSS with custom properties, layers and a naming convention
Debug layout, specificity and responsive problems in DevTools

modules.goal: Understand what CSS is, why it exists and how the browser turns a stylesheet into a painted page.

<html lang="en">
<head>

debug.title: A class selector that matches nothing
debug.error: Selector typo: the class is title but the rule says titel, so no element matches and the heading stays default.
debug.fixedOutput: Broken — heading in red.

debug.title: CSS written outside a style element
debug.error: Raw CSS in the head is text: the parser moves it into the body, so the rule is displayed instead of applied.
debug.fixedOutput: Page — heading in red; no stray CSS text on the page.

debug.title: A declaration with no colon
debug.error: Missing colon: the declaration is invalid and dropped, while the rest of the stylesheet still applies.
debug.fixedOutput: Title — heading in red.

interviewBank.q: What is CSS and why is it separate from HTML?
interviewBank.answer: CSS is the style language that describes how structured content should be presented. Keeping it separate lets one stylesheet serve many pages, lets the browser cache it, and lets a design change without editing content.

interviewBank.q: What does the cascade actually mean?
interviewBank.answer: When several rules target the same element, the browser resolves them by importance, origin, cascade layers, specificity and source order. The winner supplies each property; it is not a single whole-rule victory.

interviewBank.q: What can CSS not do on its own?
interviewBank.answer: It cannot compute business logic, store data, make network requests or respond to arbitrary input. Those need JavaScript or a server. CSS only reacts to states the browser exposes, such as hover, focus and media conditions.

interviewBank.q: What does the "C" in CSS describe?
interviewBank.answer: It names the cascade: when several rules set the same property, the browser resolves them by importance, origin, cascade layer, specificity and source order instead of picking one at random.

interviewBank.q: Which three structures does a browser combine before it can paint?
interviewBank.answer: It builds the DOM from the HTML, the CSSOM from the stylesheets, and the render tree from the nodes that will actually be painted.

interviewBank.q: What is the CSSOM?
interviewBank.answer: The CSS Object Model is the parsed, object-shaped form of every stylesheet the document loaded, which the browser can match against DOM nodes.

interviewBank.q: Why can a stylesheet delay the first paint?
interviewBank.answer: The browser treats CSS as render-blocking: painting before the styles arrive would show an unstyled page that then jumps, so it waits for the CSSOM.

interviewBank.q: What are user-agent styles?
interviewBank.answer: They are the browser's own default stylesheet — the margins on a paragraph and the size of an h1 come from it, not from the page author.

interviewBank.q: Why is CSS called a declarative language?
interviewBank.answer: You describe the result you want for a selector; you do not write the steps the browser must follow to compute or paint it.

interviewBank.q: What is the practical difference between content and presentation?
interviewBank.answer: Content is the meaning carried by the markup; presentation is the set of choices about how that meaning is shown, and CSS holds only the second.

interviewBank.q: Why does disabling CSS still leave a readable document?
interviewBank.answer: Because well-written HTML carries its meaning in elements and text, so the browser can present an unstyled but usable version without any stylesheet.

interviewBank.q: What is progressive enhancement in CSS terms?
interviewBank.answer: Ship a usable baseline first, then add layout, colour and motion behind features or queries that support them, so a failure removes polish instead of the content.

interviewBank.q: Why separate structure and style when a team works on one page?
interviewBank.answer: It lets content and design change independently, keeps one source of truth for repeated styling, and makes both parts reviewable without touching the other.

interviewBank.q: Is CSS a programming language?
interviewBank.answer: No: it has no general variables-and-control-flow model for business logic, no input or output, and no way to persist state; it is a stylesheet language with a narrow computation model.

interviewBank.q: What kind of calculation can CSS actually do?
interviewBank.answer: It can compute lengths and colours with functions such as calc, min, max and clamp, but it cannot loop over data or branch on values supplied at runtime.

interviewBank.q: What does source order decide in the cascade?
interviewBank.answer: When importance, origin, layer and specificity are all equal, the declaration that appears later in the final order wins the property.

interviewBank.q: What is inheritance in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: For properties that inherit, an element with no declaration of its own takes the computed value from its parent instead of the property's initial value.

interviewBank.q: Name three properties that inherit by default.
interviewBank.answer: color, font-family and line-height inherit, which is why setting body typography styles the whole page without repeating a rule on every element.

interviewBank.q: Name a property that does not inherit and explain the consequence.
interviewBank.answer: margin does not inherit, so a margin on a container never applies to its children and each child needs its own spacing decision.

interviewBank.q: Why does the box model matter before choosing a selector?
interviewBank.answer: A selector only decides which elements are affected; the box model decides how much space those elements occupy, so a layout bug is often a box decision rather than a matching problem.

interviewBank.q: Why does an unstyled page usually show a serif font?
interviewBank.answer: Most user-agent stylesheets set a default serif family, and the page has not yet supplied a font stack of its own.

interviewBank.q: What is a style sheet origin?
interviewBank.answer: It is who supplied the CSS: the browser's user-agent sheet, the reader's user sheet, or the page author's sheet, and the origin participates in cascade priority.

interviewBank.q: Name the three author-level ways to attach CSS to a document.
interviewBank.answer: An external stylesheet linked in the head, an internal style block, and an inline style attribute on one element.

interviewBank.q: Why do browsers ship experimental CSS behind flags?
interviewBank.answer: The specification may still change, so a flag lets implementers gather feedback and lets developers test without exposing the behaviour to every site by default.

interviewBank.q: What is a vendor prefix and what does it signal?
interviewBank.answer: A prefix such as -webkit- marks an early implementation of a property; it signals that the syntax may differ from the eventual standard and needs a fallback.

interviewBank.q: When is a vendor prefix appropriate?
interviewBank.answer: Only when a required browser version needs it, with the unprefixed declaration present as well, so the prefixed rule can be removed when support arrives.

interviewBank.q: What does feature detection mean for CSS?
interviewBank.answer: The stylesheet checks whether a feature is supported, usually with @supports, and applies the enhancement only where the browser can honour it.

interviewBank.q: How is progressive enhancement different from graceful degradation?
interviewBank.answer: Enhancement starts from a working baseline and adds capability upward; degradation starts from the full experience and tries to keep it usable when something is missing.

interviewBank.q: Why is "CSS3" not a single specification?
interviewBank.answer: CSS was split into independent modules — Grid, Color, Fonts, Media Queries — each with its own level and maturity, so there is no one CSS3 document to implement.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS module in the standards sense?
interviewBank.answer: It is a separate specification for one area of styling that can advance through levels without waiting for every other area.

interviewBank.q: What does the browser do with a property it does not know?
interviewBank.answer: It drops that declaration and continues, so the rest of the rule and the rest of the stylesheet still apply.

interviewBank.q: Why is dropping an invalid declaration safer than rejecting the whole file?
interviewBank.answer: It keeps old browsers usable while new CSS is added, and it lets a single typo fail locally instead of blanking an entire page.

interviewBank.q: How does CSS affect accessibility beyond colour?
interviewBank.answer: It controls focus visibility, text size and spacing, motion, reading order on screen, and whether controls remain usable at zoom or in forced-colours mode.

interviewBank.q: Why is semantic HTML the best base for styling?
interviewBank.answer: Elements that already describe their role give stable, meaningful selectors and remain understandable to assistive technology even before the CSS loads.

interviewBank.q: Why is colour contrast a CSS responsibility?
interviewBank.answer: The author chooses the foreground and background values, and those two values determine the contrast ratio a reader actually experiences.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS reset for?
interviewBank.answer: It removes or normalises inconsistent user-agent defaults so the design starts from a predictable baseline across browsers.

interviewBank.q: Why is a design token better than a repeated literal?
interviewBank.answer: One named value is reused everywhere, so a rebrand or theme change is a single edit and the light and dark versions cannot drift apart.

interviewBank.q: What makes a stylesheet maintainable?
interviewBank.answer: Predictable naming, a small set of tokens, deliberate cascade layers and low specificity, so a new rule can be added without guessing what it will fight.

interviewBank.q: Why is CSS difficult to scale across a large team?
interviewBank.answer: Selectors are global by default, so two people can style the same class from different files and only the cascade decides which intent survives.

interviewBank.q: What is critical CSS?
interviewBank.answer: The subset of styles needed for the first screenful, often inlined in the head so the first paint does not wait for the full stylesheet request.

interviewBank.q: Why can unused CSS still cost performance?
interviewBank.answer: Every byte must be downloaded and parsed before the CSSOM is complete, and render-blocking CSS delays the first paint whether or not its rules match anything.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between layout and paint?
interviewBank.answer: Layout computes each box's geometry and position; paint fills those boxes with pixels, so a change to geometry can force both stages.

interviewBank.q: Name two properties whose animation forces layout.
interviewBank.answer: Animating width or top changes geometry on every frame, which makes the browser recompute layout instead of only compositing.

interviewBank.q: Why is transform cheaper than top for movement?
interviewBank.answer: A transform can be handled by the compositor without re-running layout, while top changes the box's position in layout on each frame.

interviewBank.q: What can CSS animate without any JavaScript?
interviewBank.answer: Transitions and keyframe animations can move, fade, scale and colour elements in response to states such as hover, focus or a class change.

interviewBank.q: Where does JavaScript still have to take over?
interviewBank.answer: For business logic, data fetching, complex state machines and interactions that depend on values CSS cannot read, CSS states alone are not enough.

defenseBank.q: A beginner asks why not put every style inline.
defenseBank.answer: Inline styles cannot be reused, cached or overridden cleanly, and they mix presentation into the content. One external stylesheet keeps the design in a single reviewable place.
steps: Show the same rule repeated on three pages.
Point out the cache and the single edit.

defenseBank.q: Why teach HTML before CSS?
defenseBank.answer: CSS targets structure. Without knowing elements, nesting and attributes there is nothing meaningful to select, and every example becomes unexplained magic.
steps: Show a selector matching a node.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain the presentation layer?
defenseBank.answer: The page is a document with meaning; CSS is the set of decisions about how that meaning is displayed. Changing the decisions does not change the document.
steps: Turn CSS off and show the content.
Turn it on and show the design.
Point out the HTML never changed.

mcqBank.q: What does CSS stand for?
mcqBank.why: CSS is the Cascading Style Sheets language.

mcqBank.q: Which property changes the colour of text?
mcqBank.why: The color property sets the foreground text colour.

mcqBank.q: Which task is NOT CSS responsibility?
mcqBank.why: Persisting data needs JavaScript or a server.

interviewBank.q: Why is an external stylesheet preferred over a style block?
interviewBank.answer: One file can serve every page, the browser caches it across navigation, and the design lives in one reviewable place. A style block is page-specific and has to be repeated.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between file:// and a local server for CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A file URL gives every page an opaque origin and can block modules and fetch, while a local server serves the project over HTTP with the same root-relative behaviour as production.

interviewBank.q: What does the Styles panel show that the source does not?
interviewBank.answer: The live cascade: every rule that matched, which declarations won, which were overridden, and the computed value after inheritance and units are resolved.

interviewBank.q: What is the minimum file set for a styled page?
interviewBank.answer: One HTML document with a link to one CSS file is enough; the stylesheet can contain every rule the page needs.

interviewBank.q: Why keep stylesheets in a css folder?
interviewBank.answer: A predictable folder keeps relative paths short and consistent across pages, and separates authored styles from markup and assets.

interviewBank.q: How is a relative path resolved?
interviewBank.answer: It is resolved against the URL of the document that contains it, so the same href works only while the page and the target keep that relationship.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between /css/style.css and css/style.css?
interviewBank.answer: The leading slash starts at the site root; the version without it starts at the current document's folder.

interviewBank.q: Why does an absolute file path break after deployment?
interviewBank.answer: It names a location on the author's own machine, which does not exist on the server or on a visitor's device.

interviewBank.q: What does rel="stylesheet" tell the browser?
interviewBank.answer: It declares the linked resource's relationship: this file is a stylesheet to load and apply to the document.

interviewBank.q: What kinds of values can href take?
interviewBank.answer: A URL or a relative path, including a data URL, though a normal external file is what caching and review depend on.

interviewBank.q: Why does the stylesheet's MIME type matter?
interviewBank.answer: The browser applies a file served as text/css; a wrong type such as text/plain can make it fetch the file but refuse to treat it as CSS.

interviewBank.q: What happens when the CSS request returns 404?
interviewBank.answer: The document still renders, but unstyled, and the Network panel and console show the failed request instead of a silent success.

interviewBank.q: Why does a page still render when its CSS is missing?
interviewBank.answer: HTML parsing does not depend on the stylesheet, so the browser paints the document with user-agent defaults while the CSS request fails.

interviewBank.q: How do you confirm a stylesheet actually loaded?
interviewBank.answer: Find its row in the Network panel for a 200 response, then confirm its rules appear in the Styles panel for a matching element.

interviewBank.q: What does the Network panel's status column tell you?
interviewBank.answer: The HTTP result for each request: 200 means the file arrived, 304 means it was revalidated from cache, and 404 means the path is wrong.

interviewBank.q: What does the Styles panel show that the source file does not?
interviewBank.answer: The live cascade: every matching rule, which declarations won, which were overridden, and the order the browser actually applied.

interviewBank.q: What does the Computed panel show?
interviewBank.answer: The resolved value of each property after inheritance, units and functions have been evaluated, which is the number the layout engine used.

interviewBank.q: Why hard-refresh after changing CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A hard refresh bypasses the cached copy and forces a fresh request, which proves whether the change or the cache is responsible.

interviewBank.q: How does browser caching affect CSS updates?
interviewBank.answer: Until the cached response expires or is revalidated, the browser can keep applying the old stylesheet even though the server has a newer file.

interviewBank.q: What is cache busting?
interviewBank.answer: Changing the URL — a content hash or a version query — so the browser treats the file as a new resource and downloads it.

interviewBank.q: Why do build tools put a hash in CSS filenames?
interviewBank.answer: The hashed URL can be cached forever, and a new build produces a new URL automatically instead of relying on users to clear a cache.

interviewBank.q: How is file:// different from a local HTTP server for CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A file URL gives pages an opaque origin with restricted fetch and font behaviour, while a local server matches the origin rules of production.

interviewBank.q: Why can file:// break web fonts?
interviewBank.answer: Font requests are CORS-mode requests, and an opaque file origin cannot satisfy the same access rules a served page uses.

interviewBank.q: What is the viewport meta tag for?
interviewBank.answer: It tells a mobile browser to use the device width as the layout viewport instead of a virtual desktop width, which makes media queries behave as designed.

interviewBank.q: Why should the stylesheet link sit in the head?
interviewBank.answer: The browser discovers it before rendering the body, so the first paint can already use the correct styles.

interviewBank.q: What happens if the link is placed in the body?
interviewBank.answer: It usually still applies, but discovery is later, so the page can flash unstyled and the first paint is delayed by a resource found too late.

interviewBank.q: Can one page load more than one stylesheet?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, and all of them apply; their order, specificity and layers decide which declaration wins when they overlap.

interviewBank.q: How is the winner decided between two stylesheets?
interviewBank.answer: Normal cascade rules apply: importance, origin, layer and specificity first, then the order the sheets were loaded for ties.

interviewBank.q: What is @import and why is it slower than link?
interviewBank.answer: It loads another stylesheet from inside CSS, so the browser discovers it only after parsing the first file, creating a serial request chain.

interviewBank.q: What is stylesheet preloading?
interviewBank.answer: A preload hint fetches a resource earlier without applying it, which can warm the cache before the stylesheet link is reached.

interviewBank.q: What is the media attribute on a link used for?
interviewBank.answer: It conditionally applies the stylesheet, such as print-only rules or a sheet limited to a screen width range.

interviewBank.q: How do you provide a print stylesheet?
interviewBank.answer: Link a sheet with media="print" or wrap print rules in @media print inside the main stylesheet.

interviewBank.q: What is an alternate stylesheet?
interviewBank.answer: A sheet linked with rel="alternate stylesheet" and a title, which the browser offers as an optional theme rather than applying by default.

interviewBank.q: Why are filenames case-sensitive on some servers?
interviewBank.answer: Linux filesystems distinguish Style.css from style.css, so a link that works on a case-insensitive machine can 404 after deployment.

interviewBank.q: Why avoid spaces in asset filenames?
interviewBank.answer: Spaces must be percent-encoded, and a missed encoding in HTML, CSS or a build step produces a broken path that is hard to spot.

interviewBank.q: How does url() resolve inside a CSS file?
interviewBank.answer: It resolves relative to the stylesheet's own location, not the HTML document, which is why moving a CSS file can break its images.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS source map?
interviewBank.answer: A file that maps minified or compiled CSS back to the authored source, so DevTools can show the original rule and line.

interviewBank.q: Why keep source maps out of production?
interviewBank.answer: They expose original source structure and add bytes; they are a debugging aid, not part of the shipped design.

interviewBank.q: What does CSS validation catch?
interviewBank.answer: Syntax errors, unknown properties and invalid values; it cannot tell you whether the design is readable or the selector is a good idea.

interviewBank.q: What does live reload do, and what does it not catch?
interviewBank.answer: It refreshes the page when a file changes, but it does not catch a selector that matches nothing or a layout that breaks at another width.

interviewBank.q: Why configure the editor for the project?
interviewBank.answer: Consistent encoding, line endings and formatting prevent noisy diffs and stop a saved file from changing bytes nobody meant to touch.

interviewBank.q: What does a formatting convention prevent?
interviewBank.answer: It keeps diffs focused on real changes, makes missing semicolons visible, and stops reviewers from arguing about whitespace.

interviewBank.q: Why keep stylesheets in version control?
interviewBank.answer: History shows why a rule changed, review catches accidental overrides, and a bad deploy can be reverted to a known stylesheet.

interviewBank.q: What should a CSS code review check?
interviewBank.answer: Selector scope, token reuse, specificity, responsive behaviour, focus states, dead rules, and whether the change belongs in a shared file.

interviewBank.q: What is a performance budget for CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A limit on bytes, requests or render-blocking time that a change must respect, so performance is a review criterion instead of an afterthought.

interviewBank.q: What belongs in a project setup checklist?
interviewBank.answer: The correct link and path, a valid MIME type, a fresh cache, a working dev server, and confirmation in DevTools that the rules actually match.

defenseBank.q: A learner edits CSS but sees no change.
defenseBank.answer: I check the file is saved, the link path resolves, and the browser is not serving a cached stylesheet before touching the rule.
steps: Read the network entry for the CSS file.

defenseBank.q: Why not use an absolute file path in href?
defenseBank.answer: It works only on that machine and breaks for every visitor and on every deploy. A relative path travels with the project.
steps: Show the absolute path in the source.
Replace it with a relative one.

defenseBank.q: How do you explain rel="stylesheet"?
defenseBank.answer: It tells the browser what the linked file is for. Without it the file is just a resource, not a stylesheet to apply.

mcqBank.q: Which rel value links a stylesheet?
mcqBank.why: rel="stylesheet" is what makes the file a stylesheet.

mcqBank.q: Where does the link element belong?
mcqBank.why: Stylesheet links are metadata and belong in the head.

mcqBank.q: Which file extension does a browser apply as CSS?
mcqBank.why: The server sends .css as text/css and the browser applies it.

interview.answer: A hard refresh bypasses the cached copy and forces a fresh request, which proves whether the change or the cache is responsible.

interview.q: How does browser caching affect CSS updates?
interview.answer: Until the cached response expires or is revalidated, the browser can keep applying the old stylesheet even though the server has a newer file.

interview.q: What is cache busting?
interview.answer: Changing the URL — a content hash or a version query — so the browser treats the file as a new resource and downloads it.

interview.q: Why do build tools put a hash in CSS filenames?
interview.answer: The hashed URL can be cached forever, and a new build produces a new URL automatically instead of relying on users to clear a cache.

interview.q: How is file:// different from a local HTTP server for CSS?
interview.answer: A file URL gives pages an opaque origin with restricted fetch and font behaviour, while a local server matches the origin rules of production.

interview.q: Why can file:// break web fonts?
interview.answer: Font requests are CORS-mode requests, and an opaque file origin cannot satisfy the same access rules a served page uses.

interview.q: What is the viewport meta tag for?
interview.answer: It tells a mobile browser to use the device width as the layout viewport instead of a virtual desktop width, which makes media queries behave as designed.

interview.q: Why should the stylesheet link sit in the head?
interview.answer: The browser discovers it before rendering the body, so the first paint can already use the correct styles.

interview.q: What happens if the link is placed in the body?
interview.answer: It usually still applies, but discovery is later, so the page can flash unstyled and the first paint is delayed by a resource found too late.

interview.q: Can one page load more than one stylesheet?
interview.answer: Yes, and all of them apply; their order, specificity and layers decide which declaration wins when they overlap.

interview.q: How is the winner decided between two stylesheets?
interview.answer: Normal cascade rules apply: importance, origin, layer and specificity first, then the order the sheets were loaded for ties.

interview.q: What is @import and why is it slower than link?
interview.answer: It loads another stylesheet from inside CSS, so the browser discovers it only after parsing the first file, creating a serial request chain.

interview.q: What is stylesheet preloading?
interview.answer: A preload hint fetches a resource earlier without applying it, which can warm the cache before the stylesheet link is reached.

interview.q: What is the media attribute on a link used for?
interview.answer: It conditionally applies the stylesheet, such as print-only rules or a sheet limited to a screen width range.

interview.q: How do you provide a print stylesheet?
interview.answer: Link a sheet with media="print" or wrap print rules in @media print inside the main stylesheet.

interview.q: What is an alternate stylesheet?
interview.answer: A sheet linked with rel="alternate stylesheet" and a title, which the browser offers as an optional theme rather than applying by default.

interview.q: Why are filenames case-sensitive on some servers?
interview.answer: Linux filesystems distinguish Style.css from style.css, so a link that works on a case-insensitive machine can 404 after deployment.

interview.q: Why avoid spaces in asset filenames?
interview.answer: Spaces must be percent-encoded, and a missed encoding in HTML, CSS or a build step produces a broken path that is hard to spot.

interview.q: How does url() resolve inside a CSS file?
interview.answer: It resolves relative to the stylesheet's own location, not the HTML document, which is why moving a CSS file can break its images.

interview.q: What is a CSS source map?
interview.answer: A file that maps minified or compiled CSS back to the authored source, so DevTools can show the original rule and line.

interview.q: Why keep source maps out of production?
interview.answer: They expose original source structure and add bytes; they are a debugging aid, not part of the shipped design.

interview.q: What does CSS validation catch?
interview.answer: Syntax errors, unknown properties and invalid values; it cannot tell you whether the design is readable or the selector is a good idea.

interview.q: What does live reload do, and what does it not catch?
interview.answer: It refreshes the page when a file changes, but it does not catch a selector that matches nothing or a layout that breaks at another width.

interview.q: Why configure the editor for the project?
interview.answer: Consistent encoding, line endings and formatting prevent noisy diffs and stop a saved file from changing bytes nobody meant to touch.

interview.q: What does a formatting convention prevent?
interview.answer: It keeps diffs focused on real changes, makes missing semicolons visible, and stops reviewers from arguing about whitespace.

interview.q: Why keep stylesheets in version control?
interview.answer: History shows why a rule changed, review catches accidental overrides, and a bad deploy can be reverted to a known stylesheet.

interview.q: What should a CSS code review check?
interview.answer: Selector scope, token reuse, specificity, responsive behaviour, focus states, dead rules, and whether the change belongs in a shared file.

interview.q: What is a performance budget for CSS?
interview.answer: A limit on bytes, requests or render-blocking time that a change must respect, so performance is a review criterion instead of an afterthought.

interview.q: What belongs in a project setup checklist?
interview.answer: The correct link and path, a valid MIME type, a fresh cache, a working dev server, and confirmation in DevTools that the rules actually match.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a rule and a declaration?
interviewBank.answer: A rule is a selector plus a declaration block. A declaration is one property-value pair inside that block, ended by a semicolon.

interviewBank.q: What happens when one declaration is invalid?
interviewBank.answer: Only that declaration is dropped. The rest of the rule and the rest of the stylesheet still apply, which is why a typo can look like a completely missing rule.

interviewBank.q: How do CSS comments work?
interviewBank.answer: They start with slash-star and end with star-slash, may span lines, and cannot be nested. The browser removes them before parsing.

interviewBank.q: What are the parts of a CSS rule?
interviewBank.answer: A selector, an opening brace, one or more declarations made of a property, a colon and a value, then a closing brace.

interviewBank.q: How does a selector list behave?
interviewBank.answer: Each comma-separated selector matches independently; the declaration block applies to the union of everything any selector matches.

interviewBank.q: What separates one declaration from the next?
interviewBank.answer: A semicolon ends each declaration, and the final one before a closing brace may be omitted.

interviewBank.q: Why is the colon required in a declaration?
interviewBank.answer: It separates the property name from its value; without it the parser cannot tell where the name ends.

interviewBank.q: When is the last semicolon optional?
interviewBank.answer: Immediately before a closing brace, but keeping it means a later insertion cannot accidentally join two declarations.

interviewBank.q: What is a declaration block?
interviewBank.answer: The braces and their contents that hold all the declarations applied by the selector before them.

interviewBank.q: What is an at-rule, and name three.
interviewBank.answer: A statement beginning with @ that controls how CSS is processed, such as @media, @supports and @keyframes.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a shorthand and a longhand?
interviewBank.answer: A shorthand sets several longhand properties at once, while a longhand sets exactly one.

interviewBank.q: Why can a shorthand reset values you did not mention?
interviewBank.answer: It assigns every longhand it owns, using the initial value for any part you omitted, so it can wipe an earlier declaration.

interviewBank.q: What happens when one rule contains the same property twice?
interviewBank.answer: Both declarations are valid, and the later one wins for that property.

interviewBank.q: Why does whitespace matter in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: It separates tokens; outside strings and selectors its amount is insignificant, but removing it where a separator is required changes the parse.

interviewBank.q: Are CSS property names case-sensitive?
interviewBank.answer: No, standard property names are ASCII case-insensitive, although custom properties and some values are case-sensitive.

interviewBank.q: Are class names case-sensitive?
interviewBank.answer: Yes in HTML documents, so .Card and .card are different selectors and only one will match the markup.

interviewBank.q: How do you write a comment that spans several lines?
interviewBank.answer: Start with slash-star, write across as many lines as needed, and end with star-slash.

interviewBank.q: Why can CSS comments not be nested?
interviewBank.answer: The first star-slash closes the comment, so an inner opening is just text and the following code can be swallowed or exposed.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS function?
interviewBank.answer: A value form with a name and parentheses, such as rgb(), calc() or var(), which the browser evaluates while computing the property.

interviewBank.q: What is calc() used for?
interviewBank.answer: It performs arithmetic across compatible units at computed-value time, such as subtracting fixed padding from a percentage width.

interviewBank.q: What happens when var() references a missing property?
interviewBank.answer: The fallback is used if one is supplied; otherwise the declaration becomes invalid at computed-value time.

interviewBank.q: What does "invalid at computed-value time" mean?
interviewBank.answer: The declaration parsed but its substituted value is not valid for the property, so the property takes its inherited or initial value instead.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between initial and inherited values?
interviewBank.answer: initial is the value defined by the specification; inherited is the parent's computed value, used only for properties that inherit.

interviewBank.q: What does the inherit keyword force?
interviewBank.answer: It makes the element take its parent's computed value even for a property that normally does not inherit.

interviewBank.q: What does the unset keyword do?
interviewBank.answer: It resets an inherited property to inherit and a non-inherited property to its initial value.

interviewBank.q: What does the revert keyword do?
interviewBank.answer: It discards the current origin or layer's value and falls back to the value from the previous origin in the cascade.

interviewBank.q: What does the all property do?
interviewBank.answer: It resets almost every property at once, except direction and unicode-bidi, which are excluded for writing-mode reasons.

interviewBank.q: Why is all: unset risky?
interviewBank.answer: It wipes every property, including ones a component relied on, and the resulting element is hard to debug because nothing in its own rules explains the state.

interviewBank.q: How does the CSS parser recover from an error?
interviewBank.answer: It skips the malformed declaration or rule and resumes at the next boundary, so one mistake does not stop the rest of the file.

interviewBank.q: Why does one broken rule not blank the page?
interviewBank.answer: Error recovery is part of the language: the browser drops only the invalid construct and keeps the valid rules around it.

interviewBank.q: How do you find a declaration the browser dropped?
interviewBank.answer: Look for it in the Styles panel; a missing or struck-through declaration and a console warning usually identify the invalid value.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS escape sequence for?
interviewBank.answer: It represents a character that would otherwise be ambiguous in an identifier or string, such as a digit at the start of a class name.

interviewBank.q: Is @charset still required?
interviewBank.answer: Rarely: an HTTP charset or a meta charset on the HTML document covers most cases, and @charset must be the very first bytes to count.

interviewBank.q: What is @namespace used for?
interviewBank.answer: It binds a prefix to an XML namespace so selectors can target elements in documents such as inline SVG or XUL.

interviewBank.q: What does the & selector mean in nesting?
interviewBank.answer: It refers to the parent selector, which lets a nested rule build compound selectors and pseudo-classes without repeating the parent.

interviewBank.q: Why does a nested rule need a parent?
interviewBank.answer: Nesting resolves relative to the enclosing rule, so without one there is no selector for & or the implicit descendant relationship to attach to.

interviewBank.q: How is a custom property different from a normal property?
interviewBank.answer: It stores an arbitrary token stream, inherits by default, and is substituted only when var() uses it, so it has no type until then.

interviewBank.q: Why can a custom property hold an apparently invalid value?
interviewBank.answer: Its contents are not validated at declaration time; validity is checked when the value is substituted into a real property.

interviewBank.q: What does minification remove from CSS?
interviewBank.answer: Comments and insignificant whitespace, and it may shorten values, while preserving the cascade and the meaning of each declaration.

interviewBank.q: Why does minification not change which rule wins?
interviewBank.answer: It removes bytes, not selectors or order, so the same declarations remain in the same cascade positions.

interviewBank.q: How does source order work inside one rule?
interviewBank.answer: For duplicate declarations of the same property, the last valid one in the block wins.

interviewBank.q: How do specificity and source order interact?
interviewBank.answer: Specificity decides first; source order only breaks a tie when specificity, origin, importance and layer are equal.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a syntax error and a semantic error?
interviewBank.answer: A syntax error breaks the parse; a semantic error parses but uses an unknown property or a value the property cannot accept, so it is dropped later.

interviewBank.q: Why is color: red valid but color red not?
interviewBank.answer: The colon is the required separator between property and value, and without it the parser has no declaration to accept.

interviewBank.q: What makes a declaration invalid?
interviewBank.answer: An unknown property, a value of the wrong type or unit, a missing colon, or a function whose arguments do not fit the grammar.

interviewBank.q: What is the fastest way to learn CSS syntax?
interviewBank.answer: Write small complete documents, change one declaration at a time, and read the Styles panel to see exactly what the browser accepted or dropped.

defenseBank.q: A learner asks whether the last semicolon is required.
defenseBank.answer: It is optional before a closing brace but I keep it, because inserting another declaration later is the common edit and a missing semicolon then breaks two declarations at once.
steps: Show a rule without the last semicolon.

defenseBank.q: Why insist on one property per line?
defenseBank.answer: Diffs become readable, a missing semicolon is visible, and review comments can point at one line. Minification is the build step’s job.

defenseBank.q: Why does the browser not show a syntax error?
defenseBank.answer: CSS error handling is designed to recover: it drops the bad declaration and continues. DevTools shows the surviving rules, not the ones that were discarded.
steps: Fix it and watch it appear.

mcqBank.q: Which part of a rule chooses the elements?
mcqBank.why: The selector is the part before the braces.

mcqBank.q: Which is valid CSS comment syntax?
mcqBank.why: CSS only supports slash-star block comments.

mcqBank.q: What does a missing closing brace usually cause?
mcqBank.why: The parser keeps reading until it finds a closing brace.

interview.q: What is the difference between a rule and a declaration?
interview.answer: A rule is a selector plus a declaration block. A declaration is one property-value pair inside that block, ended by a semicolon.

interview.q: What happens when one declaration is invalid?
interview.answer: Only that declaration is dropped. The rest of the rule and the rest of the stylesheet still apply, which is why a typo can look like a completely missing rule.

interview.q: How do CSS comments work?
interview.answer: They start with slash-star and end with star-slash, may span lines, and cannot be nested. The browser removes them before parsing.

interview.q: What are the parts of a CSS rule?
interview.answer: A selector, an opening brace, one or more declarations made of a property, a colon and a value, then a closing brace.

interview.q: How does a selector list behave?
interview.answer: Each comma-separated selector matches independently; the declaration block applies to the union of everything any selector matches.

interview.q: What separates one declaration from the next?
interview.answer: A semicolon ends each declaration, and the final one before a closing brace may be omitted.

interview.q: Why is the colon required in a declaration?
interview.answer: It separates the property name from its value; without it the parser cannot tell where the name ends.

interview.q: When is the last semicolon optional?
interview.answer: Immediately before a closing brace, but keeping it means a later insertion cannot accidentally join two declarations.

interview.q: What is a declaration block?
interview.answer: The braces and their contents that hold all the declarations applied by the selector before them.

interview.q: What is an at-rule, and name three.
interview.answer: A statement beginning with @ that controls how CSS is processed, such as @media, @supports and @keyframes.

interview.q: What is the difference between a shorthand and a longhand?
interview.answer: A shorthand sets several longhand properties at once, while a longhand sets exactly one.

interview.q: Why can a shorthand reset values you did not mention?
interview.answer: It assigns every longhand it owns, using the initial value for any part you omitted, so it can wipe an earlier declaration.

interview.q: What happens when one rule contains the same property twice?
interview.answer: Both declarations are valid, and the later one wins for that property.

interview.q: Why does whitespace matter in CSS?
interview.answer: It separates tokens; outside strings and selectors its amount is insignificant, but removing it where a separator is required changes the parse.

interview.q: Are CSS property names case-sensitive?
interview.answer: No, standard property names are ASCII case-insensitive, although custom properties and some values are case-sensitive.

interview.q: Are class names case-sensitive?
interview.answer: Yes in HTML documents, so .Card and .card are different selectors and only one will match the markup.

interview.q: How do you write a comment that spans several lines?
interview.answer: Start with slash-star, write across as many lines as needed, and end with star-slash.

interview.q: Why can CSS comments not be nested?
interview.answer: The first star-slash closes the comment, so an inner opening is just text and the following code can be swallowed or exposed.

interview.q: What is a CSS function?
interview.answer: A value form with a name and parentheses, such as rgb(), calc() or var(), which the browser evaluates while computing the property.

interview.q: What is calc() used for?
interview.answer: It performs arithmetic across compatible units at computed-value time, such as subtracting fixed padding from a percentage width.

interview.q: What happens when var() references a missing property?
interview.answer: The fallback is used if one is supplied; otherwise the declaration becomes invalid at computed-value time.

interview.q: What does "invalid at computed-value time" mean?
interview.answer: The declaration parsed but its substituted value is not valid for the property, so the property takes its inherited or initial value instead.

interview.q: What is the difference between initial and inherited values?
interview.answer: initial is the value defined by the specification; inherited is the parent's computed value, used only for properties that inherit.

interview.q: What does the inherit keyword force?
interview.answer: It makes the element take its parent's computed value even for a property that normally does not inherit.

interview.q: What does the unset keyword do?
interview.answer: It resets an inherited property to inherit and a non-inherited property to its initial value.

interview.q: What does the revert keyword do?
interview.answer: It discards the current origin or layer's value and falls back to the value from the previous origin in the cascade.

interview.q: What does the all property do?
interview.answer: It resets almost every property at once, except direction and unicode-bidi, which are excluded for writing-mode reasons.

interview.q: Why is all: unset risky?
interview.answer: It wipes every property, including ones a component relied on, and the resulting element is hard to debug because nothing in its own rules explains the state.

interview.q: How does the CSS parser recover from an error?
interview.answer: It skips the malformed declaration or rule and resumes at the next boundary, so one mistake does not stop the rest of the file.

interview.q: Why does one broken rule not blank the page?
interview.answer: Error recovery is part of the language: the browser drops only the invalid construct and keeps the valid rules around it.

interview.q: How do you find a declaration the browser dropped?
interview.answer: Look for it in the Styles panel; a missing or struck-through declaration and a console warning usually identify the invalid value.

interview.q: What is a CSS escape sequence for?
interview.answer: It represents a character that would otherwise be ambiguous in an identifier or string, such as a digit at the start of a class name.

interview.q: Is @charset still required?
interview.answer: Rarely: an HTTP charset or a meta charset on the HTML document covers most cases, and @charset must be the very first bytes to count.

interview.q: What is @namespace used for?
interview.answer: It binds a prefix to an XML namespace so selectors can target elements in documents such as inline SVG or XUL.

interview.q: What does the & selector mean in nesting?
interview.answer: It refers to the parent selector, which lets a nested rule build compound selectors and pseudo-classes without repeating the parent.

interview.q: Why does a nested rule need a parent?
interview.answer: Nesting resolves relative to the enclosing rule, so without one there is no selector for & or the implicit descendant relationship to attach to.

interview.q: How is a custom property different from a normal property?
interview.answer: It stores an arbitrary token stream, inherits by default, and is substituted only when var() uses it, so it has no type until then.

interview.q: Why can a custom property hold an apparently invalid value?
interview.answer: Its contents are not validated at declaration time; validity is checked when the value is substituted into a real property.

interview.q: What does minification remove from CSS?
interview.answer: Comments and insignificant whitespace, and it may shorten values, while preserving the cascade and the meaning of each declaration.

interview.q: Why does minification not change which rule wins?
interview.answer: It removes bytes, not selectors or order, so the same declarations remain in the same cascade positions.

interview.q: How does source order work inside one rule?
interview.answer: For duplicate declarations of the same property, the last valid one in the block wins.

interview.q: How do specificity and source order interact?
interview.answer: Specificity decides first; source order only breaks a tie when specificity, origin, importance and layer are equal.

interview.q: What is the difference between a syntax error and a semantic error?
interview.answer: A syntax error breaks the parse; a semantic error parses but uses an unknown property or a value the property cannot accept, so it is dropped later.

interview.q: Why is color: red valid but color red not?
interview.answer: The colon is the required separator between property and value, and without it the parser has no declaration to accept.

interview.q: What makes a declaration invalid?
interview.answer: An unknown property, a value of the wrong type or unit, a missing colon, or a function whose arguments do not fit the grammar.

interview.q: What is the fastest way to learn CSS syntax?
interview.answer: Write small complete documents, change one declaration at a time, and read the Styles panel to see exactly what the browser accepted or dropped.

interviewBank.q: Why is external CSS preferred in production?
interviewBank.answer: It is cached once for many pages, keeps content and presentation apart, and allows a whole site to be restyled from one file. Inline and internal styles cannot be shared.

interviewBank.q: Which wins between inline and external CSS?
interviewBank.answer: An inline declaration wins at equal importance because the style attribute is treated as author origin with higher specificity. Only !important in the stylesheet, or a change of importance, overrides it.

interviewBank.q: How do you organise multiple stylesheets?
interviewBank.answer: Load a reset or base layer first, then the design system, then page or component styles, so later files can rely on earlier tokens and win ties deliberately.

interviewBank.q: What are the three ways to attach CSS to HTML?
interviewBank.answer: A linked external stylesheet, an internal style element in the head, and an inline style attribute on an element.

interviewBank.q: Which attachment method wins for normal author declarations?
interviewBank.answer: An inline style wins over stylesheet selectors because the style attribute participates in the author origin with higher specificity.

interviewBank.q: Why is inline CSS hard to override?
interviewBank.answer: Only a more important author declaration or a change to the attribute itself can beat it, so every later design change has to fight the markup.

interviewBank.q: When is inline CSS legitimate?
interviewBank.answer: For generated documents such as email, for a single dynamic value that cannot be expressed as a class, and for throwaway prototypes.

interviewBank.q: Why is external CSS cacheable across pages?
interviewBank.answer: Every page can reference the same URL, so the browser downloads it once and reuses the stored response on later navigations.

interviewBank.q: What does an internal style block scope to?
interviewBank.answer: The document that contains it; no other page can use those rules unless the block is duplicated there.

interviewBank.q: Can internal and external styles conflict?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, both are author styles, so the normal cascade decides which declaration wins for each property.

interviewBank.q: How is the winner decided when internal and external styles conflict?
interviewBank.answer: Specificity and layers decide first; at equal weight the later declaration in document order wins.

interviewBank.q: Why does link order matter between two themes?
interviewBank.answer: With equal specificity the later stylesheet wins, so a theme that must override another has to load after it.

interviewBank.q: What is the cascade order among author styles?
interviewBank.answer: Importance, then cascade layers, then specificity, then source order; all four can matter in one conflict.

interviewBank.q: Where do user styles sit relative to author styles?
interviewBank.answer: For normal declarations the author wins, but for important declarations the user origin wins, which is how reader overrides protect accessibility.

interviewBank.q: Why can a user stylesheet override a site?
interviewBank.answer: A user !important declaration outranks an author !important declaration, so the reader can enforce contrast or motion preferences.

interviewBank.q: What does !important do to origin order?
interviewBank.answer: It reverses the normal origin priority: important user declarations beat important author declarations, and both beat normal author styles.

interviewBank.q: Why is !important considered a last resort?
interviewBank.answer: It breaks the cascade's normal reasoning, forces the next fix to be another important rule, and hides the real specificity problem.

interviewBank.q: What specificity does the style attribute have?
interviewBank.answer: It is treated as an author declaration with a weight above any selector, so even an ID selector does not outrank it normally.

interviewBank.q: How do you override an inline style without !important?
interviewBank.answer: Change or remove the attribute, or have the element's own stylesheet declaration win through importance; selector strength alone will not do it.

interviewBank.q: Why can a style attribute not express a pseudo-class?
interviewBank.answer: It styles only the element's current state and has no selector, so :hover, :focus and media conditions are impossible inline.

interviewBank.q: Can a style attribute contain a media query?
interviewBank.answer: No, the attribute holds declarations only; responsive changes need a stylesheet rule or a script that swaps values.

interviewBank.q: Why are style attributes common in email HTML?
interviewBank.answer: Many email clients strip style elements and external links, so inline declarations are the most reliable way to carry the design.

interviewBank.q: What is CSS-in-JS?
interviewBank.answer: It authors styles inside JavaScript, usually generating scoped class names and injecting a stylesheet at runtime or build time.

interviewBank.q: What trade-off does CSS-in-JS make?
interviewBank.answer: It gains colocation and dynamic values, but adds runtime or bundle cost and can make the final cascade harder to inspect than plain CSS.

interviewBank.q: What is scoped CSS?
interviewBank.answer: A build or framework technique that adds a unique attribute or class to selectors so rules cannot leak outside their component.

interviewBank.q: How does Shadow DOM isolate styles?
interviewBank.answer: It gives a component its own tree and style scope, so page selectors do not reach in and component selectors do not leak out.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a linked stylesheet and @import?
interviewBank.answer: A link is discovered while parsing HTML and fetched in parallel; @import is discovered only after the parent stylesheet is parsed, so it is serial.

interviewBank.q: Why is @import render-blocking?
interviewBank.answer: The browser cannot finish the CSSOM until the imported sheet arrives, so the import chain delays the first paint.

interviewBank.q: How do you decide which rules belong in critical CSS?
interviewBank.answer: Take only the styles for the first screenful — its layout, type and surfaces — measured from the rendered page, never the whole stylesheet.

interviewBank.q: Why inline critical CSS in the head?
interviewBank.answer: It removes a network round trip from the first paint; the rest of the CSS can load afterwards without blocking the initial view.

interviewBank.q: What is a flash of unstyled content?
interviewBank.answer: A frame or more of unstyled HTML shown before the stylesheet applies, usually caused by late or blocked CSS discovery.

interviewBank.q: How do you prevent a flash of unstyled content?
interviewBank.answer: Put the stylesheet in the head, avoid late imports, and inline the critical rules that determine the first screen.

interviewBank.q: What makes a resource render-blocking?
interviewBank.answer: The browser must load and process it before it can paint the first frame; CSS and synchronous scripts in the head are the common cases.

interviewBank.q: Why can a large stylesheet delay the first paint?
interviewBank.answer: The CSSOM must be complete before the render tree is built, so every blocking byte adds to the time before anything can be painted.

interviewBank.q: What does media="print" do on a link?
interviewBank.answer: It marks the stylesheet for print output, so screen rendering does not apply it.

interviewBank.q: How do you test a print stylesheet?
interviewBank.answer: Use the browser's print preview or DevTools' print emulation, then check page breaks, hidden navigation and readable contrast.

interviewBank.q: Can a linked stylesheet be disabled by script?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, setting the link element's disabled property to true stops its rules from applying until it is re-enabled.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer classes over IDs for reusable styles?
interviewBank.answer: Classes can repeat, carry lower specificity and compose with other classes, while an ID is unique and hard to override.

interviewBank.q: How does a Content Security Policy affect inline styles?
interviewBank.answer: A strict style-src blocks inline style attributes and style elements unless a nonce or hash allows them, so external CSS is easier to secure.

interviewBank.q: What is Subresource Integrity for CSS?
interviewBank.answer: An integrity hash on the link lets the browser refuse a stylesheet whose bytes do not match the expected digest.

interviewBank.q: Why is SRI less common for stylesheets?
interviewBank.answer: It requires CORS-enabled responses and exact version pinning, so a CDN URL that changes breaks the hash and many teams use a bundled local copy instead.

interviewBank.q: What is the crossorigin attribute for on a link?
interviewBank.answer: It makes the browser fetch the resource in CORS mode, which is required for integrity checks and for some font requests.

interviewBank.q: Why do font requests need CORS?
interviewBank.answer: Fonts are fetched in CORS mode by specification, so the server must send the appropriate access headers or the font is blocked.

interviewBank.q: How do you migrate inline styles to a stylesheet safely?

interview.q: Why is external CSS preferred in production?
interview.answer: It is cached once for many pages, keeps content and presentation apart, and allows a whole site to be restyled from one file. Inline and internal styles cannot be shared.

interview.q: Which wins between inline and external CSS?
interview.answer: An inline declaration wins at equal importance because the style attribute is treated as author origin with higher specificity. Only !important in the stylesheet, or a change of importance, overrides it.

interview.q: How do you organise multiple stylesheets?
interview.answer: Load a reset or base layer first, then the design system, then page or component styles, so later files can rely on earlier tokens and win ties deliberately.

interview.q: What are the three ways to attach CSS to HTML?
interview.answer: A linked external stylesheet, an internal style element in the head, and an inline style attribute on an element.

interview.q: Which attachment method wins for normal author declarations?
interview.answer: An inline style wins over stylesheet selectors because the style attribute participates in the author origin with higher specificity.

interview.q: Why is inline CSS hard to override?
interview.answer: Only a more important author declaration or a change to the attribute itself can beat it, so every later design change has to fight the markup.

interview.q: When is inline CSS legitimate?
interview.answer: For generated documents such as email, for a single dynamic value that cannot be expressed as a class, and for throwaway prototypes.

interview.q: Why is external CSS cacheable across pages?
interview.answer: Every page can reference the same URL, so the browser downloads it once and reuses the stored response on later navigations.

interview.q: What does an internal style block scope to?
interview.answer: The document that contains it; no other page can use those rules unless the block is duplicated there.

interview.q: Can internal and external styles conflict?
interview.answer: Yes, both are author styles, so the normal cascade decides which declaration wins for each property.

interview.q: How is the winner decided when internal and external styles conflict?
interview.answer: Specificity and layers decide first; at equal weight the later declaration in document order wins.

interview.q: Why does link order matter between two themes?
interview.answer: With equal specificity the later stylesheet wins, so a theme that must override another has to load after it.

interview.q: What is the cascade order among author styles?
interview.answer: Importance, then cascade layers, then specificity, then source order; all four can matter in one conflict.

interview.q: Where do user styles sit relative to author styles?
interview.answer: For normal declarations the author wins, but for important declarations the user origin wins, which is how reader overrides protect accessibility.

interview.q: Why can a user stylesheet override a site?
interview.answer: A user !important declaration outranks an author !important declaration, so the reader can enforce contrast or motion preferences.

interview.q: What does !important do to origin order?
interview.answer: It reverses the normal origin priority: important user declarations beat important author declarations, and both beat normal author styles.

interview.q: Why is !important considered a last resort?
interview.answer: It breaks the cascade's normal reasoning, forces the next fix to be another important rule, and hides the real specificity problem.

interview.q: What specificity does the style attribute have?
interview.answer: It is treated as an author declaration with a weight above any selector, so even an ID selector does not outrank it normally.

interview.q: How do you override an inline style without !important?
interview.answer: Change or remove the attribute, or have the element's own stylesheet declaration win through importance; selector strength alone will not do it.

interview.q: Why can a style attribute not express a pseudo-class?
interview.answer: It styles only the element's current state and has no selector, so :hover, :focus and media conditions are impossible inline.

interview.q: Can a style attribute contain a media query?
interview.answer: No, the attribute holds declarations only; responsive changes need a stylesheet rule or a script that swaps values.

interview.q: Why are style attributes common in email HTML?
interview.answer: Many email clients strip style elements and external links, so inline declarations are the most reliable way to carry the design.

interview.q: What is CSS-in-JS?
interview.answer: It authors styles inside JavaScript, usually generating scoped class names and injecting a stylesheet at runtime or build time.

interview.q: What trade-off does CSS-in-JS make?
interview.answer: It gains colocation and dynamic values, but adds runtime or bundle cost and can make the final cascade harder to inspect than plain CSS.

interview.q: What is scoped CSS?
interview.answer: A build or framework technique that adds a unique attribute or class to selectors so rules cannot leak outside their component.

interview.q: How does Shadow DOM isolate styles?
interview.answer: It gives a component its own tree and style scope, so page selectors do not reach in and component selectors do not leak out.

interview.q: What is the difference between a linked stylesheet and @import?
interview.answer: A link is discovered while parsing HTML and fetched in parallel; @import is discovered only after the parent stylesheet is parsed, so it is serial.

interview.q: Why is @import render-blocking?
interview.answer: The browser cannot finish the CSSOM until the imported sheet arrives, so the import chain delays the first paint.

interview.q: How do you decide which rules belong in critical CSS?
interview.answer: Take only the styles for the first screenful — its layout, type and surfaces — measured from the rendered page, never the whole stylesheet.

interview.q: Why inline critical CSS in the head?
interview.answer: It removes a network round trip from the first paint; the rest of the CSS can load afterwards without blocking the initial view.

interview.q: What is a flash of unstyled content?
interview.answer: A frame or more of unstyled HTML shown before the stylesheet applies, usually caused by late or blocked CSS discovery.

interview.q: How do you prevent a flash of unstyled content?
interview.answer: Put the stylesheet in the head, avoid late imports, and inline the critical rules that determine the first screen.

interview.q: What makes a resource render-blocking?
interview.answer: The browser must load and process it before it can paint the first frame; CSS and synchronous scripts in the head are the common cases.

interview.q: Why can a large stylesheet delay the first paint?
interview.answer: The CSSOM must be complete before the render tree is built, so every blocking byte adds to the time before anything can be painted.

interview.q: What does media="print" do on a link?
interview.answer: It marks the stylesheet for print output, so screen rendering does not apply it.

interview.q: How do you test a print stylesheet?
interview.answer: Use the browser's print preview or DevTools' print emulation, then check page breaks, hidden navigation and readable contrast.

interview.q: Can a linked stylesheet be disabled by script?
interview.answer: Yes, setting the link element's disabled property to true stops its rules from applying until it is re-enabled.

interview.q: Why prefer classes over IDs for reusable styles?
interview.answer: Classes can repeat, carry lower specificity and compose with other classes, while an ID is unique and hard to override.

interview.q: How does a Content Security Policy affect inline styles?
interview.answer: A strict style-src blocks inline style attributes and style elements unless a nonce or hash allows them, so external CSS is easier to secure.

interview.q: What is Subresource Integrity for CSS?
interview.answer: An integrity hash on the link lets the browser refuse a stylesheet whose bytes do not match the expected digest.

interview.q: Why is SRI less common for stylesheets?
interview.answer: It requires CORS-enabled responses and exact version pinning, so a CDN URL that changes breaks the hash and many teams use a bundled local copy instead.

interview.q: What is the crossorigin attribute for on a link?
interview.answer: It makes the browser fetch the resource in CORS mode, which is required for integrity checks and for some font requests.

interview.q: Why do font requests need CORS?
interview.answer: Fonts are fetched in CORS mode by specification, so the server must send the appropriate access headers or the font is blocked.

interview.q: How do you migrate inline styles to a stylesheet safely?
interview.answer: Inventory each attribute, create a class with the same declarations, replace the attribute, and compare the computed styles before removing the old path.

interview.q: What should a stylesheet loading checklist include?
interview.answer: The path and rel value, the served MIME type, load order, cache state, CSP allowances, and a DevTools check that the rules match.

interview.q: How do you debug a stylesheet that loads but does not apply?
interview.answer: Check whether the selector matches, whether a more specific rule wins, whether a media query or layer excludes it, and whether the link is disabled.

interviewBank.q: When do you use a class instead of an id?
interviewBank.answer: Classes are reusable and are the default styling hook. An id is unique, so it is reserved for fragment targets, label associations and one-off references, not for styles that repeat.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a space and a child combinator?
interviewBank.answer: A space matches any descendant at any depth; > matches only elements whose direct parent is the one named. The child combinator is stricter and usually safer.

interviewBank.q: How specific is an attribute selector compared with a class?
interviewBank.answer: An attribute selector and a class selector both count as one class-level component. Specificity is equal, so source order decides between them.

interviewBank.q: What does the universal selector match, and why avoid it for styling?
interviewBank.answer: An asterisk matches every element, so a styling rule reaches places you did not consider; it is useful in a reset but too broad for component design.

interviewBank.q: What does a type selector match?
interviewBank.answer: Every element with that tag name, regardless of class or position, which makes it a good base rule and a poor way to style one instance.

interviewBank.q: How does a class selector match when an element has several classes?
interviewBank.answer: It matches when the element's class attribute contains that exact token, so an element can satisfy several independent class rules at once.

interviewBank.q: Why can an element carry more than one class?
interviewBank.answer: Classes compose: one supplies layout, another colour, another state, so behaviour can be combined without inventing a new selector for every combination.

interviewBank.q: Why is styling through IDs a problem?
interviewBank.answer: An ID is unique, cannot be reused across components, and carries specificity high enough that later variations need heavier selectors to override it.

interviewBank.q: What happens when one selector in a comma list is invalid?
interviewBank.answer: For an ordinary selector list the whole rule is dropped, because the browser cannot know which part of the list you meant.

interviewBank.q: How does the descendant combinator differ from the child combinator?
interviewBank.answer: A space matches an ancestor at any depth; a greater-than sign matches only an element whose direct parent is the named one.

interviewBank.q: When is a child combinator the safer choice?
interviewBank.answer: When a component's styles must not leak into nested copies of the same markup, since only the immediate children are affected.

interviewBank.q: What does the adjacent sibling combinator match?
interviewBank.answer: The one element that immediately follows the first, with no other element between them, such as a label directly after an input.

interviewBank.q: What does the general sibling combinator match?
interviewBank.answer: Every following sibling that matches the selector, not only the first, which is useful for a heading followed by several paragraphs.

interviewBank.q: How do you select an element that merely has an attribute?
interviewBank.answer: Write the attribute name in brackets, such as [disabled], which matches any element carrying that attribute whatever its value.

interviewBank.q: How do you select an exact attribute value?
interviewBank.answer: Use the equals form, such as [type="email"], which matches only when the value is exactly that string.

interviewBank.q: What does the prefix attribute selector do?
interviewBank.answer: [href^="https"] matches values that begin with the given text, which is a common way to mark external links.

interviewBank.q: What does the suffix attribute selector do?
interviewBank.answer: [href$=".pdf"] matches values that end with the text, useful for marking file types without adding another class.

interviewBank.q: What does the substring attribute selector do?
interviewBank.answer: [class*="promo"] matches any value containing that sequence, which is broad and should be used only when the naming is controlled.

interviewBank.q: What does the i flag change in an attribute selector?
interviewBank.answer: It makes the value comparison ASCII case-insensitive, so [type="EMAIL" i] also matches type="email".

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between a pseudo-class and a pseudo-element?
interviewBank.answer: A pseudo-class selects an element in a state or position; a pseudo-element selects or generates a part of an element, such as its first line.

interviewBank.q: What does :not() do?
interviewBank.answer: It excludes elements that match its argument, and it can be chained or given a complex list in modern browsers.

interviewBank.q: How does :is() choose its specificity?
interviewBank.answer: It takes the specificity of the most specific selector in its argument list, so it can unexpectedly raise the weight of a rule.

interviewBank.q: Why use :where() instead of :is()?
interviewBank.answer: :where() always contributes zero specificity, which makes it ideal for resets and base styles that must not outrank component rules.

interviewBank.q: What problem does :has() solve?
interviewBank.answer: It lets a selector depend on a descendant or following sibling, so a parent can be styled because of a child's state without adding a class from script.

interviewBank.q: How does :nth-child() count elements?
interviewBank.answer: It counts an element's position among all of its element siblings, so other types of siblings affect the result.

interviewBank.q: How is :nth-of-type() different?
interviewBank.answer: It counts only siblings of the same element type, so intervening paragraphs do not change which heading is selected.

interviewBank.q: When does :first-child match?
interviewBank.answer: Only when the element is the first element child of its parent; a text node before it does not count, but another element does.

interviewBank.q: What does :only-child match?
interviewBank.answer: An element that is the sole element child of its parent, which is useful for layouts with one item instead of several.

interviewBank.q: What does :empty match, and what is the common surprise?
interviewBank.answer: It matches an element with no children or text at all, and even a single whitespace character counts as text, so the element stops matching.

interviewBank.q: What is :root and how is it different from html?
interviewBank.answer: :root matches the document's root element and has class-level specificity, while the type selector html has element-level specificity.

interviewBank.q: What specificity does :has() contribute?
interviewBank.answer: It takes the specificity of its most specific argument, the same rule as :is(), so a complex argument raises the weight of the whole selector.

interviewBank.q: Why does one invalid selector break a whole selector list?
interviewBank.answer: Without forgiving syntax the parser cannot decide which list item you intended, so it discards the rule rather than applying a partial match.

interviewBank.q: Are complex selectors actually slow?
interviewBank.answer: Modern engines match right-to-left and optimise common cases, so readability and correctness matter far more than micro-optimising selector length.

interviewBank.q: Why avoid styling with IDs even when the markup has them?
interviewBank.answer: IDs cannot repeat, so the style cannot be reused, and their weight makes every variation a specificity fight instead of a class change.

interviewBank.q: What does BEM encode in a class name?
interviewBank.answer: A block, its elements with a double underscore, and modifiers with a double hyphen, so ownership and variation are readable from the markup.

interviewBank.q: Which attribute selectors are useful for form controls?
interviewBank.answer: [type="email"], [required], [disabled] and [aria-invalid="true"] let CSS react to real control state without extra classes.

interviewBank.q: What does :lang() select?
interviewBank.answer: Elements whose language matches the given value, including inherited language, so typography can change for a quoted foreign phrase.

interviewBank.q: What does :dir() select?
interviewBank.answer: Elements whose directionality is left-to-right or right-to-left, which is useful for logical layout in bilingual documents.

interviewBank.q: What does :target match?
interviewBank.answer: The element whose ID matches the URL fragment, which lets a page highlight the section a link jumped to.

interviewBank.q: What is :scope for?
interviewBank.answer: It refers to the element a selector is scoped to, such as the root of querySelectorAll or a nested style scope.

interviewBank.q: What does & mean inside a nested CSS rule?
interviewBank.answer: It stands for the parent selector, so & .child or &:hover builds the full selector without repeating the parent by hand.

interviewBank.q: What is the specificity of .nav a:hover?
interviewBank.answer: Two class-level components and one element component, written 0-2-1, because .nav and :hover each count as a class.

interviewBank.q: What is the specificity of #id .class?
interviewBank.answer: One ID and one class, written 1-1-0, so it beats any number of classes without an ID.

interviewBank.q: Why does duplicating selectors hurt maintenance?
interviewBank.answer: Each copy drifts independently, and adding a variation means finding every duplicate or raising specificity until the newest rule wins.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug a selector that matches nothing?
interviewBank.answer: Inspect the element, check the selector text against the DOM, confirm class case, and test the rule in the Styles panel before assuming the CSS file is wrong.

interviewBank.q: What does :has() change about CSS architecture?
interviewBank.answer: It allows state to flow upward from a child, which removes some classes that script used to add, but it should be treated as an enhancement where support matters.

defenseBank.q: A learner styles with ids everywhere.
defenseBank.answer: Ids cannot repeat and their specificity is hard to override, so the first variation forces a new id. Classes express reusable patterns and stay manageable.
