interviewBank.q: Hex or HSL — which do you choose and why?
interviewBank.answer: Hex is compact and familiar for fixed brand values. HSL is easier to reason about when deriving variants, because hue, saturation and lightness are separate numbers.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between background and background-color?
interviewBank.answer: background is a shorthand that resets every background property; background-color sets only the colour. Using the shorthand after a colour can wipe the earlier layer.

interviewBank.q: How do you keep text readable on a gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Check contrast against the darkest and lightest part of the gradient, add a solid overlay behind the text, and never assume the middle of a gradient is the worst case.

interviewBank.q: How does a three-digit hex colour expand?
interviewBank.answer: Each digit is doubled, so #f0a becomes #ff00aa; the shorthand is valid only when both digits of every pair are identical.

interviewBank.q: What does an eight-digit hex colour add?
interviewBank.answer: The final pair is alpha, so #2563ebcc is the blue #2563eb at roughly eighty percent opacity.

interviewBank.q: What is the space-separated rgb() syntax?
interviewBank.answer: It writes channels without commas and puts alpha after a slash, such as rgb(37 99 235 / 0.8), which is the modern form.

interviewBank.q: How is hsl() written?
interviewBank.answer: Hue in degrees, saturation and lightness as percentages, with optional alpha after a slash, such as hsl(221 83% 53% / 0.9).

interviewBank.q: What does the color() function allow?
interviewBank.answer: It selects an explicit colour space, such as display-p3, which can express colours outside the sRGB gamut on capable displays.

interviewBank.q: Why use oklch() instead of hsl()?
interviewBank.answer: OKLCH is perceptually uniform, so changing lightness or hue behaves more predictably and a palette keeps even contrast steps.

interviewBank.q: What does color-mix() do?
interviewBank.answer: It blends two colours in a chosen colour space, which is useful for deriving hover or tint variants from a single token.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between opacity and an alpha colour?
interviewBank.answer: opacity fades the whole element including its children and border, while an alpha colour fades only that one paint.

interviewBank.q: What does currentColor refer to?
interviewBank.answer: It resolves to the element's computed color, so a border or icon can follow the text colour without repeating the value.

interviewBank.q: Is transparent the same as a transparent black?
interviewBank.answer: transparent is a named colour equal to transparent black, but using it as a background can still change how blending and shadows behave.

interviewBank.q: Why are named colours risky for a design system?
interviewBank.answer: Names are limited and inconsistent across palettes, so a brand token expressed as a name is harder to adjust and version than a value.

interviewBank.q: What is a contrast ratio?
interviewBank.answer: A ratio between the relative luminance of two colours, from 1:1 to 21:1, used to judge whether text is readable against its background.

interviewBank.q: What contrast does WCAG AA require for normal text?
interviewBank.answer: At least 4.5:1 for normal-size text, measured between the text colour and the actual background behind it.

interviewBank.q: What contrast is required for large text?
interviewBank.answer: At least 3:1, because larger glyphs remain legible at a lower ratio than body-size text.

interviewBank.q: What does background-color set?
interviewBank.answer: The solid colour painted behind an element's content and padding, below any background image and inside the border box.

interviewBank.q: How do multiple background images stack?
interviewBank.answer: The first layer in the list paints on top, and later layers paint beneath it, so an overlay gradient is written before the photo.

interviewBank.q: What does background-repeat control?
interviewBank.answer: Whether and how an image tiles across the background; no-repeat shows one copy, while repeat-x or repeat-y tiles in one direction.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between background-size cover and contain?
interviewBank.answer: cover fills the box and may crop the image, while contain shows the whole image and may leave empty space.

interviewBank.q: What does background-position do?
interviewBank.answer: It places the image within the painting area, using keywords, lengths or percentages, often combined with cover to choose the crop focus.

interviewBank.q: What does background-attachment: fixed do?
interviewBank.answer: It fixes the background to the viewport so it does not move with the element's scroll, an effect that is often expensive on mobile.

interviewBank.q: Why is the background shorthand dangerous after setting a colour?
interviewBank.answer: It resets every background longhand it owns, so a later shorthand without a colour can wipe the colour you set earlier.

interviewBank.q: How do you set the direction of a linear gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Use an angle or a side keyword, such as linear-gradient(135deg, ...) or linear-gradient(to right, ...), before the colour stops.

interviewBank.q: How is a radial gradient positioned?
interviewBank.answer: Its centre and shape are set before the stops, such as radial-gradient(circle at 30% 30%, ...), which changes where the colour bloom begins.

interviewBank.q: What is a conic gradient useful for?
interviewBank.answer: It sweeps colour around a centre point, which suits pie charts, colour wheels and angular progress indicators.

interviewBank.q: What is a colour stop?
interviewBank.answer: A colour paired with an optional position along the gradient line, which tells the browser where that colour must be reached.

interviewBank.q: What is a hard stop in a gradient?
interviewBank.answer: Two stops at the same position create an abrupt edge instead of a blend, which can draw stripes or a sharp split background.

interviewBank.q: When do you use a repeating gradient?
interviewBank.answer: When a small pattern must tile across a larger area, such as stripes or a progress track, using repeating-linear-gradient with a short cycle.

interviewBank.q: Why does a gradient sometimes show banding?
interviewBank.answer: Too few colour steps across a large area reveal the 8-bit quantization, which can be reduced with subtle noise, dithering or a smoother colour space.

interviewBank.q: How do you place text over a photo reliably?
interviewBank.answer: Paint a semi-transparent gradient or solid overlay as the top background layer, then choose a text colour that contrasts with the darkest part of that overlay.

interviewBank.q: Why set a background colour when using a background image?
interviewBank.answer: If the image fails or loads slowly, the fallback colour keeps the text on a deliberate surface instead of the browser default.

interviewBank.q: What does background-blend-mode do?
interviewBank.answer: It blends an element's background layers with each other, such as multiplying a texture into a colour, without affecting the content above them.

interviewBank.q: How is filter different from backdrop-filter?
interviewBank.answer: filter affects the element's own rendering, while backdrop-filter blurs or adjusts whatever is painted behind the element.

interviewBank.q: How do you design colours for dark mode?
interviewBank.answer: Define semantic tokens, then override their values in a dark scope; pure inversion is avoided because saturated colours and shadows behave differently on dark surfaces.

interviewBank.q: What are CSS system colours?
interviewBank.answer: Keywords such as Canvas and CanvasText that follow the user's operating-system theme, which help a page fit forced-colours and high-contrast modes.

interviewBank.q: What is forced-colors mode?
interviewBank.answer: A user setting where the browser replaces author colours with a limited system palette, so designs must keep borders, focus and meaning visible without colour alone.

interviewBank.q: Why does print need different colour decisions?
interviewBank.answer: Printers handle ink and paper differently, backgrounds are often not printed, and light text on a dark background can become unreadable or waste ink.

interviewBank.q: What is colour management in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: The browser maps declared colours into the display's colour space, which is why a wide-gamut P3 colour can look different from the same sRGB value.

interviewBank.q: Why keep a palette of raw colour tokens?
interviewBank.answer: A small named palette gives one place to adjust values, while components reference semantic tokens built from it instead of inventing new hex codes.

interviewBank.q: What is a semantic colour token?
interviewBank.answer: A name that describes a role, such as surface or danger, rather than a hue, so the value can change with theme while the meaning stays stable.

interviewBank.q: Which tools help verify contrast?
interviewBank.answer: Browser DevTools' contrast readout, dedicated contrast checkers and automated accessibility audits, always measured against the real rendered background.

interviewBank.q: How do you make gradient text?
interviewBank.answer: Clip the background to the text and make the text transparent, but keep a solid fallback because the technique can fail in forced-colours or older engines.

interviewBank.q: Why can large background images hurt performance?
interviewBank.answer: They add download and decode cost, and a fixed or repainting background can force expensive work during scroll, especially on mobile GPUs.

interviewBank.q: Why is colour alone a poor way to convey meaning?
interviewBank.answer: Readers with colour-vision deficiency, monochrome screens or forced-colours mode lose the distinction, so pair colour with text, icons, weight or pattern.

defenseBank.q: A learner picks colours by eye only.
defenseBank.answer: I check contrast with a tool, because a colour that looks fine on one monitor fails for low-vision users and in bright light.

defenseBank.q: Why set a fallback background colour with an image?
defenseBank.answer: If the image fails or is slow, the text still sits on a deliberate surface instead of the browser default.
steps: Show the page with images blocked.

mcqBank.q: Which format supports transparency directly?
mcqBank.why: The slash syntax adds alpha to rgb.

mcqBank.q: In HSL, what does the H stand for?
mcqBank.why: Hue is the colour angle on the wheel.

interviewBank.q: rem or em — when do you use each?
interviewBank.answer: rem for anything that should follow the root scale: type, spacing, radii. em when a component should scale relative to its own font size, such as padding on a button.

interviewBank.q: Why can 100vw cause a horizontal scrollbar?
interviewBank.answer: On desktop vw includes the vertical scrollbar width, while the content area does not. 100% follows the containing block and avoids the mismatch.

interviewBank.q: What does clamp actually do?
interviewBank.answer: clamp(min, preferred, max) returns the preferred value, but never below the minimum or above the maximum. It is the standard way to make type fluid without media queries.

interviewBank.q: What is a CSS pixel?
interviewBank.answer: A logical unit resolved against the display's reference pixel, not a guarantee of one physical device pixel, which is why high-density screens scale it.

interviewBank.q: What does rem measure?
interviewBank.answer: The root element's computed font size, so one rem follows the user's base size instead of a hard-coded pixel value.

interviewBank.q: What does em measure?
interviewBank.answer: The element's own computed font size, or its parent's when used on font-size, which makes it relative and sometimes compounding.

interviewBank.q: A percentage width resolves against what?
interviewBank.answer: The containing block's width, so the same fifty percent is a different number of pixels in a narrow and a wide parent.

interviewBank.q: When are vw and vh useful?
interviewBank.answer: For sizes that should follow the viewport, such as a full-height hero or fluid type, though vw includes the scrollbar on desktop.

interviewBank.q: What do dvh, svh and lvh solve?
interviewBank.answer: They separate the dynamic, small and large viewport heights on mobile, where browser chrome changes the visible area during scroll.

interviewBank.q: When do vmin and vmax help?
interviewBank.answer: When a square or shape must follow the shorter or longer viewport side, so it stays proportional in both portrait and landscape.

interviewBank.q: What does the ch unit represent?
interviewBank.answer: The width of the zero glyph in the current font, which makes it a useful approximation for limiting a line to a number of characters.

interviewBank.q: What does ex measure?
interviewBank.answer: The x-height of the current font, a font-relative unit that is rarely used except for small optical adjustments.

interviewBank.q: What does fr mean in a grid track?
interviewBank.answer: A fraction of the free space left after fixed tracks and gaps, so 1fr and 2fr split that space in a one-to-two ratio.

interviewBank.q: Which CSS units are absolute?
interviewBank.answer: px, cm, mm, in, pt and pc are absolute in CSS terms, though px is still resolved against the reference pixel rather than a device dot.

interviewBank.q: When are physical units such as cm or pt still appropriate?
interviewBank.answer: For print stylesheets and documents that must match paper dimensions, not for screen layout where zoom and density vary.

interviewBank.q: What is the default root font size?
interviewBank.answer: Sixteen CSS pixels in most browsers, but it is a user preference, so rem-based layouts must not assume that number is fixed.

interviewBank.q: How does browser zoom interact with px and rem?
interviewBank.answer: Zoom scales the whole layout, but a user's font-size preference changes the root size, which rem respects and px ignores for text.

interviewBank.q: Why does nested em sizing compound?
interviewBank.answer: Each level multiplies its parent's computed size, so two nested 1.2em elements produce 1.44 times the outer size instead of 1.2.

interviewBank.q: Why is line-height better left unitless?
interviewBank.answer: A unitless value multiplies the element's own font size, so nested text keeps the intended ratio instead of inheriting a fixed length.

interviewBank.q: What does calc() require around plus and minus?
interviewBank.answer: Whitespace on both sides of the operator, because without it the parser can read the sign as part of a number or identifier.

interviewBank.q: What does min() choose?
interviewBank.answer: The smallest of its arguments, allowing a width to shrink below a preferred value but never exceed a hard limit.

interviewBank.q: What does max() choose?
interviewBank.answer: The largest of its arguments, which is useful for a minimum size that still grows with available space.

interviewBank.q: What are the three parts of clamp()?
interviewBank.answer: A minimum, a preferred value and a maximum; the browser returns the preferred value bounded by the other two.

interviewBank.q: What does minmax() do in a grid track?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a track's minimum and maximum size, so a column can shrink no further than the first value and grow no larger than the second.

interviewBank.q: How does fit-content behave?
interviewBank.answer: It sizes to the content up to a limit, then stops growing, which is useful for chips and sidebars that should not stretch.

interviewBank.q: What does auto mean for width and height?
interviewBank.answer: It lets the browser resolve the size from the layout context, such as filling a block or sizing to content, rather than a fixed number.

interviewBank.q: Why is zero allowed without a unit?
interviewBank.answer: Zero is the same length in every unit, so the specification permits the bare number while other nonzero lengths require a unit.

interviewBank.q: What does percentage padding resolve against?
interviewBank.answer: The containing block's inline size, even for vertical padding, which is why percentage padding can create surprising aspect ratios.

interviewBank.q: Why does percentage height often fail?
interviewBank.answer: It needs a definite containing block height; if the parent's height is auto, the percentage has nothing to resolve against and is treated as auto.

interviewBank.q: What does aspect-ratio do?
interviewBank.answer: It sets a preferred width-to-height ratio, letting one dimension follow the other while the box remains responsive.

interviewBank.q: What are container query units?
interviewBank.answer: Units such as cqw and cqh that resolve against the nearest query container instead of the viewport, so a component can scale with its own space.

interviewBank.q: Can media queries use rem?
interviewBank.answer: Yes, and doing so ties breakpoints to the user's root font size, so a reader who enlarges text gets the layout intended for a wider screen.

interviewBank.q: Why keep borders in px?
interviewBank.answer: A one-pixel border usually expresses a hairline regardless of text size, while spacing and type should follow the user's scale.

interviewBank.q: What are resolution units used for?
interviewBank.answer: dpi, dpcm and dppx describe pixel density, mainly in media queries for choosing sharper images on high-density displays.

interviewBank.q: What are angle units used for?
interviewBank.answer: deg, grad, rad and turn describe rotation and gradient direction, with turn being a convenient full circle.

interviewBank.q: What are time units used for?
interviewBank.answer: s and ms set transition and animation durations and delays; they are the only units accepted for those properties.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer fr over percentages in a grid?
interviewBank.answer: fr distributes the space left after gaps and fixed tracks, so tracks do not overflow when gaps are added.

interviewBank.q: Why are viewport units unreliable for mobile height?
interviewBank.answer: Mobile browser chrome changes the visible height during scroll, so vh can be taller than the actual visible area; dvh or svh reflect that behaviour.

interviewBank.q: How do you create fluid type?
interviewBank.answer: Use clamp() with a viewport-relative preferred value, bounded by a readable minimum and maximum, instead of fixing a size per breakpoint.

interviewBank.q: How do you create fluid spacing?
interviewBank.answer: Use clamp() or calc() on a spacing token, so gaps grow with the viewport within limits rather than jumping at breakpoints.

interviewBank.q: How do you convert between px and rem?
interviewBank.answer: Divide the pixel value by the root font size, usually sixteen, so 24px becomes 1.5rem; the conversion is a design aid, not a runtime rule.

interviewBank.q: Why can a px-based design fail accessibility?
interviewBank.answer: The text ignores the reader's font-size preference, so a user who enlarges text still sees the original size and may be unable to read it.

interviewBank.q: Why use rem for spacing as well as text?
interviewBank.answer: Spacing tied to the root scale keeps the rhythm proportional when the reader changes text size, instead of leaving cramped gaps around larger type.

interviewBank.q: Why is ch useful for a reading measure?
interviewBank.answer: A width in ch approximates characters per line, so a 65ch limit keeps a comfortable measure even when the font size changes.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug a unit mismatch?
interviewBank.answer: Inspect the Computed panel for the resolved pixel value, then trace which parent or font size the relative unit resolved against.

interviewBank.q: Which unit should a beginner default to?
interviewBank.answer: rem for type and spacing, percentages or fr for layout, and px for hairlines, then reach for viewport and container units only when the layout needs them.

defenseBank.q: A design uses px for every font size.
defenseBank.answer: px ignores the user’s font-size preference, which breaks zoom and accessibility. rem follows the root size and respects that setting.
steps: Change the browser default font size.
Switch to rem and show it scale.

defenseBank.q: Why is a unitless line-height safer?
defenseBank.answer: A unitless value multiplies the element’s own font size, so nested text keeps the intended ratio. A px line-height stays fixed and can overlap when the font grows.
steps: Show a large heading with 20px line-height.

mcqBank.q: What does 1rem equal by default?
mcqBank.why: The default root font size is 16px.

mcqBank.q: Which unit shares free space in a Grid track?
mcqBank.why: fr distributes the free space of the grid container.

interviewBank.q: Why does font-family take a list?
interviewBank.answer: The browser uses the first family it can actually render. The list ends with a generic family so the page never falls back to an unrelated default.

interviewBank.q: Why is line-height usually unitless?
interviewBank.answer: A unitless number multiplies the element’s own font size, so it scales with nested text instead of staying a fixed length.

interviewBank.q: What is FOUT and how do you reduce it?
interviewBank.answer: Flash of unstyled text: fallback text is shown before the web font loads, then swaps. Preloading the font, using font-display and choosing a close fallback reduce the visible shift.

interviewBank.q: Why does font-family take an ordered stack?
interviewBank.answer: The browser uses the first family it can render, so the order decides which available font wins before the generic fallback is reached.

interviewBank.q: Why must every stack end in a generic family?
interviewBank.answer: A generic family is guaranteed to exist, so the page still gets a sensible serif, sans-serif or monospace instead of the browser's arbitrary default.

interviewBank.q: What is a web font?
interviewBank.answer: A font file delivered by the page and declared with @font-face, which gives a consistent typeface instead of relying on installed fonts.

interviewBank.q: What does @font-face declare?
interviewBank.answer: A font family name, one or more sources with formats, and descriptors such as weight, style and display behaviour.

interviewBank.q: What does font-display control?
interviewBank.answer: How a web font behaves while it loads: swap shows fallback text immediately, block hides text briefly, and optional avoids late swaps.

interviewBank.q: Why preload a font file?
interviewBank.answer: Preloading starts the request before the CSS that references it is parsed, which reduces the delay before the first text paint.

interviewBank.q: What is a flash of invisible text?
interviewBank.answer: A period where the browser hides text while waiting for a web font, usually caused by a block period in font-display.

interviewBank.q: What do numeric font-weight values mean?
interviewBank.answer: They range from 100 to 900 in increasing boldness, and a variable font can interpolate between them instead of jumping to named weights.

interviewBank.q: What is a variable font?
interviewBank.answer: A single font file with axes for weight, width or slant, so the page can request intermediate values without downloading several files.

interviewBank.q: What does font-style control?
interviewBank.answer: Whether the face is normal, italic or oblique, and the browser may synthesise a slant if the family lacks a real italic.

interviewBank.q: Why use a type scale instead of arbitrary sizes?
interviewBank.answer: A small set of related sizes creates hierarchy and rhythm, while one-off font sizes make the page look uneven and hard to maintain.

interviewBank.q: Why express type sizes in rem?
interviewBank.answer: rem follows the reader's root preference, so the whole scale grows together when the default font size is increased.

interviewBank.q: What does line-height: normal mean?
interviewBank.answer: The font's own recommended line spacing, which varies by typeface and is rarely the value a designer wants for body text.

interviewBank.q: What is a readable measure?
interviewBank.answer: Roughly 45 to 75 characters per line, often limited with ch, because lines that are too long or too short slow reading.

interviewBank.q: What does letter-spacing change?
interviewBank.answer: The space between characters; small positive values can help uppercase labels, while large values hurt word recognition.

interviewBank.q: What does word-spacing change?
interviewBank.answer: The space between words, which is rarely adjusted except for justified text or a specific display treatment.

interviewBank.q: What does text-align affect?
interviewBank.answer: The alignment of inline content inside its block, such as left, right, center or justify, not the position of the block itself.

interviewBank.q: How do you remove an underline from a link accessibly?
interviewBank.answer: Remove it only when another clear affordance remains, and always keep a visible focus and hover state so the link is still recognisable.

interviewBank.q: What does text-transform do?
interviewBank.answer: It changes the rendered case without changing the underlying text, so uppercase labels remain readable to screen readers and copy-paste.

interviewBank.q: How does text-shadow differ from box-shadow?
interviewBank.answer: text-shadow follows the glyph shapes and takes no spread or inset value, while box-shadow follows the element's box.

interviewBank.q: What does text-overflow require to work?
interviewBank.answer: A single-line box with overflow hidden and white-space nowrap, otherwise the text wraps and there is no overflow to ellipsise.

interviewBank.q: What does white-space control?
interviewBank.answer: Whether whitespace collapses, wraps or is preserved, which decides if text stays on one line or breaks at spaces.

interviewBank.q: What does overflow-wrap: anywhere do?
interviewBank.answer: It allows a long unbreakable string to break at any point when needed, preventing it from forcing the container wider.

interviewBank.q: How is word-break different from overflow-wrap?
interviewBank.answer: word-break changes the language's normal breaking rules, while overflow-wrap only intervenes when a word would otherwise overflow.

interviewBank.q: What does hyphens: auto do?
interviewBank.answer: It lets the browser insert language-aware hyphenation at line ends, which can improve justification but needs the correct lang attribute.

interviewBank.q: What does text-wrap: balance do?
interviewBank.answer: It distributes lines evenly in a short block such as a heading, avoiding a single orphan word on the last line.

interviewBank.q: What does font-variant control?
interviewBank.answer: It selects alternate glyph sets such as small caps or old-style numerals, a higher-level switch than raw font features.

interviewBank.q: How do you enable tabular numbers?
interviewBank.answer: Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits share a width, which keeps columns of figures aligned.

interviewBank.q: How do you style a drop cap?
interviewBank.answer: Use ::first-letter with a larger size and float, then check the line box so the cap does not collide with the first line.

interviewBank.q: What is vertical rhythm?
interviewBank.answer: A consistent baseline spacing derived from line-height, so headings, paragraphs and margins land on the same grid instead of drifting.

interviewBank.q: How do you make type responsive without breakpoints?
interviewBank.answer: Use clamp() with a viewport-relative middle value and a readable minimum and maximum, then test the extremes.

interviewBank.q: Why cap fluid type with clamp()?
interviewBank.answer: Without a maximum, headings become absurdly large on wide screens; without a minimum, body text becomes unreadable on small ones.

interviewBank.q: What text spacing does WCAG expect?
interviewBank.answer: Readers must be able to increase line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing and word spacing without losing content or functionality.

interviewBank.q: Why is text contrast more than a colour choice?
interviewBank.answer: The final ratio depends on the actual background, overlays and states, so a colour that passes on white can fail on an image or a tinted card.

interviewBank.q: How do web fonts affect performance?
interviewBank.answer: They add requests and bytes, can delay text, and may cause layout shift when the fallback and web font have different metrics.

interviewBank.q: Why use system fonts on some projects?
interviewBank.answer: They load instantly, match the platform and avoid layout shift, which is often the better trade-off for utility interfaces.

interviewBank.q: Why prefer SVG icons over an icon font?
interviewBank.answer: SVG icons are individually accessible, styleable and crisp at any size, while icon fonts depend on private-use glyphs and can fail silently.

interviewBank.q: What are fallback font metrics?
interviewBank.answer: The measurements used to match a fallback closely to the web font, reducing the size and position shift when the real font swaps in.

interviewBank.q: When should a font be self-hosted?
interviewBank.answer: When the project needs control over privacy, caching and licensing, or the third-party font service is a performance or reliability risk.

interviewBank.q: What does font-smoothing change?
interviewBank.answer: It alters glyph antialiasing on some platforms, which can make text look thinner or heavier but is not a reliable cross-browser design control.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug a typography problem?
interviewBank.answer: Inspect the computed font family, size and line height, then check whether a fallback rendered, a rule was overridden, or the measure is wrong.

interviewBank.q: What are OpenType features in CSS?
interviewBank.answer: Optional glyph behaviours such as ligatures, fractions or stylistic sets, enabled with font-feature-settings or higher-level font-variant properties.

interviewBank.q: Why limit a paragraph with ch rather than px?
interviewBank.answer: ch scales with the font, so the measure stays proportional when the reader changes text size instead of becoming too wide or too narrow.

defenseBank.q: A learner sets body text to 12px to fit more.
defenseBank.answer: Small text costs readability and fails accessibility expectations. A 16px base with a wider measure and tighter spacing fits content without shrinking it.

defenseBank.q: Why cap the line length?
defenseBank.answer: Long lines make the eye lose its place on the return sweep; very short lines break rhythm. A 60–75 character measure is the readable range.

mcqBank.q: Which is a generic font family?
mcqBank.why: Generic families are the guaranteed fallbacks.

mcqBank.q: Which property adds space between letters?
mcqBank.why: letter-spacing adjusts space between characters.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between content-box and border-box?
interviewBank.answer: content-box adds padding and border outside the declared width. border-box includes them inside it, so width means the visible box. Most projects set border-box globally.

interviewBank.q: Why do vertical margins collapse?
interviewBank.answer: Adjacent block margins in normal flow combine into the larger of the two instead of adding, and a parent and first child can collapse too. Padding, borders, flex or grid contexts stop it.

defenseBank.q: A learner sets width 100% and gets a scrollbar.
defenseBank.answer: The padding and border are being added outside the width. border-box makes the declared width include them, which is why it is the usual global reset.

defenseBank.q: Why not use margins for inner spacing?
defenseBank.answer: Margin is outside the border and can collapse with neighbours; padding is inside and belongs to the element’s own surface.
steps: Show a background that stops at the padding.

mcqBank.q: Which value includes padding and border in the declared width?
mcqBank.why: border-box makes width the visible box.

mcqBank.q: Which side is outside the border?
mcqBank.why: Margin is the outermost spacing layer.

interviewBank.q: display:none or visibility:hidden — which do you use?
interviewBank.answer: display:none removes the element from layout, accessibility and tab order. visibility:hidden keeps the space but hides the element. Choose by whether the space should exist.

interviewBank.q: What does inline-block give you that inline does not?
interviewBank.answer: It stays in the text flow like an inline box but accepts width, height and vertical margins, which makes it useful for chips and older nav patterns.

defenseBank.q: A learner tries to center a span with width.
defenseBank.answer: An inline box ignores width. Make it inline-block or put the centring on the block parent instead.

defenseBank.q: Why prefer flex over inline-block for navigation?
defenseBank.answer: Flex handles gaps, alignment and wrapping without whitespace artefacts between inline-blocks, and it keeps working when labels change length.

mcqBank.q: What is the default display of a div?
mcqBank.why: A div is a block-level element by default.

mcqBank.q: Which value removes an element from layout entirely?
mcqBank.why: Only display:none removes the box from layout.

topics.title: A border needs width, style and colour
topics.body: Border shorthand teen cheezein leta hai. Sirf width aur colour likhne se style default none rehta hai aur border dikhta hi nahi.
topics.code:
Full border
Top border only
topics.output: First box has a 2px blue border and 10px radius; second has only a 4px amber top border.

topics.title: Outline sits outside the border
topics.body: Outline layout me jagah nahi leta aur radius follow nahi karta. Focus indicators ke liye yahi use hota hai, border ki jagah nahi.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">

interviewBank.q: Outline or border for focus?
interviewBank.answer: Outline, because it does not affect layout, can be offset from the edge, and is designed for focus indication. Removing it without a replacement breaks keyboard accessibility.

interviewBank.q: Why layer two box shadows?
interviewBank.answer: A tight, darker shadow suggests contact while a wide, lighter one suggests ambient light. Together they read as real depth without looking like a blurry halo.

defenseBank.q: A designer asks for a 1px border that does not change size.
defenseBank.answer: A border adds to the box unless border-box is set. With border-box the border is drawn inside the declared width and the layout stays put.

defenseBank.q: Why not use box-shadow instead of a border?
defenseBank.answer: A shadow is paint only; it does not define the element’s edge, does not print reliably and cannot replace the visual boundary for high-contrast users.
steps: Show the shadow in forced colours.

mcqBank.q: Which border style must be present for a border to paint?
mcqBank.why: A visible style such as solid is required.

mcqBank.q: Which shadow draws inside the element?
mcqBank.why: The inset keyword draws the shadow inside the box.

interviewBank.q: What containing block does an absolute element use?
interviewBank.answer: The nearest ancestor with a position other than static, or a transform, filter or container-type that establishes one. Without such an ancestor it uses the initial containing block.

interviewBank.q: How is sticky different from fixed?
interviewBank.answer: Sticky stays in normal flow until the scroll reaches its inset threshold, then behaves as if fixed within its containing block. Fixed is always relative to the viewport.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses absolute for the whole page layout.
defenseBank.answer: Absolute removes elements from flow, so nothing reserves their space and overlapping is inevitable. Flow, flex or grid should own layout; absolute is for overlays and badges.

defenseBank.q: Why does a huge z-index still sit behind?

interviewBank.q: Flexbox or Grid — how do you choose?
interviewBank.answer: Flexbox distributes items along one axis and is content-driven. Grid defines rows and columns together and is layout-driven. Use flex for a bar or a row of chips, grid for a page or gallery.

interviewBank.q: Why does a flex item refuse to shrink?
interviewBank.answer: A flex item’s automatic minimum size is its content size, so long unbreakable content can prevent shrinking. min-width:0 (or overflow handling) lets it shrink below that.

defenseBank.q: A learner centres with margins.
defenseBank.answer: auto margins work in flex but are less explicit than justify-content and fail in wrapping or multi-line cases. Alignment properties express the intent.
steps: Add a second line and compare.

defenseBank.q: Why set gap instead of margins between items?
defenseBank.answer: Gap belongs to the container, so it does not add space at the outer edges and does not collapse. Margins have to be undone on the first or last child.

mcqBank.q: Which property aligns items on the cross axis?
mcqBank.why: align-items works across the cross axis.

mcqBank.q: What does flex: 1 mean?
mcqBank.why: It is the common shorthand for equal flexible items.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between auto-fit and auto-fill?
interviewBank.answer: auto-fill keeps empty tracks and leaves blank space; auto-fit collapses empty tracks so the existing items stretch to fill the row. Galleries usually want auto-fit.

interviewBank.q: What is the implicit grid?
interviewBank.answer: Tracks the browser creates automatically when items are placed outside the explicit template. It is why an extra item still lands somewhere sensible.

defenseBank.q: A learner uses flex for a two-dimensional page.
defenseBank.answer: Flex aligns along one axis; a page with a header, sidebar and main area is two-dimensional. Grid expresses the rows and columns directly.

defenseBank.q: Why use minmax in a gallery?
defenseBank.answer: It sets a floor so tiles never get too narrow and a ceiling of 1fr so they share the remaining space, which removes the need for breakpoints.

mcqBank.q: Which unit distributes free space in a grid?
mcqBank.why: The fr unit represents a fraction of the free space.

mcqBank.q: Which property names a grid area?
mcqBank.why: grid-area assigns an item to a named area or line span.

interviewBank.q: Why mobile-first?
interviewBank.answer: The base styles target the smallest, most constrained layout, and min-width queries add capability. It keeps the default CSS simple and avoids undoing desktop rules on small screens.

interviewBank.q: When is a container query better than a media query?
interviewBank.answer: When a component’s layout depends on its own available width rather than the viewport — a card in a sidebar and the same card in a wide main column should adapt independently.

defenseBank.q: A learner picks breakpoints from device names.
defenseBank.answer: Devices change every year and the layout only cares about its own width. I resize until the content breaks, then put the query there.
steps: Add the query at that width.

defenseBank.q: Why set max-width 100% on images?
defenseBank.answer: An image with intrinsic width larger than its container overflows and causes horizontal scrolling. max-width plus height auto keeps it fluid and proportional.

mcqBank.q: Which query targets screens at least 640px wide?
mcqBank.why: min-width matches that width and above.

mcqBank.q: Which meta tag is required for mobile layout?
mcqBank.why: Without it mobile browsers use a virtual desktop width.

topics.title: Interaction states
topics.body: hover, active aur focus-visible user interaction ke states hain. focus-visible keyboard focus par lagta hai, isliye mouse click par unnecessary ring nahi aata.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>States</title>
  <style>
    .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; }
    .btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8; }
    .btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); }
    .btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Save</button>
</body>
</html>

interviewBank.q: :focus or :focus-visible?
interviewBank.answer: :focus matches every focus, including a mouse click. :focus-visible matches when the browser judges that focus should be visible, which is usually keyboard navigation. Use it for rings.

interviewBank.q: Why does :where exist when :is can do the same grouping?
interviewBank.answer: :where always contributes zero specificity, which makes it ideal for resets and base styles that must not outrank component rules.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants the focus ring removed.
defenseBank.answer: The ring is the only signal a keyboard user has. We can restyle it to match the brand, but not remove it.

defenseBank.q: When is :has the right tool?
defenseBank.answer: When a parent must react to a child’s state and no class is being set by script, such as marking a field wrapper invalid. Where script already sets a class, that class is simpler.

mcqBank.q: Which pseudo-class matches every second list item?
mcqBank.why: 2n matches positions 2, 4, 6 and so on.

mcqBank.q: Which selector adds no specificity?
mcqBank.why: :where() always has zero specificity.

interviewBank.q: Why does ::before need a content property?
interviewBank.answer: Generated boxes only exist when content is set, even an empty string. Without it the pseudo-element has no box to style.

interviewBank.q: Is generated content accessible?
interviewBank.answer: It is read by some screen readers depending on the content and browser, and it is not reliably selectable or translatable. Real content belongs in the markup.

defenseBank.q: A learner puts the entire button label in ::before.
defenseBank.answer: If the generated content fails, the control has no label, and it may not be exposed correctly. The label belongs in the markup; pseudo-elements are decoration.
steps: Move the label into the element.

defenseBank.q: Why prefer a real element over an overlay pseudo-element?
defenseBank.answer: A pseudo-element cannot receive events or be individually selected or announced, so anything interactive needs a real element.

modules.title: CSS Transitions and Transformations
modules.goal: Animate state changes smoothly and move, rotate, scale or skew elements without affecting layout.

topics.title: Transitions need four decisions
topics.body: Transition property, duration, timing function aur delay batata hai. Sirf un properties par lagta hai jinke beech browser interpolate kar sakta hai.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Transition</title>
  <style>
    .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; transition: background-color 180ms ease, transform 180ms ease; }
    .btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8; transform: translateY(-2px); }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Hover me</button>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Button darkens and lifts 2px over 180ms on hover; it does not jump.

topics.title: Transform moves without reflow
topics.body: translate, rotate, scale aur skew element ko paint stage par badalte hain, isliye aas-paas ka layout nahi hilta. Multiple functions ek hi transform me likho.
topics.code: Lift on hover
topics.output: Card rises 4px and scales up 1% smoothly; the surrounding layout stays in place.

topics.title: Transform origin and 3D
topics.body: transform-origin rotation ka centre badalta hai. perspective aur rotateX/rotateY depth ka illusion dete hain, lekin overuse motion sickness bhi de sakta hai.
topics.code: Rotate from the left
topics.output: Badge rotates slightly anticlockwise from its left edge and grows 5% on hover.

debug.title: A transition on display none
debug.broken:
<style>
  .panel { display: none; transition: opacity 200ms ease; }
  .panel.open { display: block; opacity: 1; }
</style>
debug.fix:
<style>
  .panel { opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 200ms ease, visibility 200ms; }
  .panel.open { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }
</style>
debug.error: display is not interpolable: the element jumps from no box to a box, so there are no intermediate frames to transition.
debug.fixedOutput: Panel fades in over 200ms.

debug.title: Two transform declarations that cancel each other
debug.error: Duplicate property: the second declaration overrides the first, so the card scales but never moves.
debug.fixedOutput: Card rises and scales together.

tasks.title: A card that lifts on hover
tasks.statement: Build a card with a 200ms transform transition, a 4px lift and a slightly stronger shadow on hover.
tasks.solution: Hover to lift
tasks.expected: White card that rises 4px and gains a deeper shadow over 200ms on hover.

interviewBank.q: Which properties are cheap to animate?
interviewBank.answer: transform and opacity, because they can be handled on the compositor without layout or paint. Animating width, top or box-shadow forces more work each frame.

interviewBank.q: What does transform do to layout?
interviewBank.answer: Nothing. It changes the visual rendering after layout, so neighbours do not move and the original space is preserved.

defenseBank.q: A learner animates width for a progress bar.
defenseBank.answer: Animating width triggers layout on every frame. A transform scaleX on an inner bar gives the same visual with far less work.
steps: Show the layout cost in DevTools.

defenseBank.q: Why respect reduced motion?
defenseBank.answer: Large movement and parallax can cause nausea and vestibular symptoms. A prefers-reduced-motion query should remove or shorten non-essential motion.

mcqBank.q: Which property defines how long a transition takes?
mcqBank.why: Duration is the time the transition runs.

mcqBank.q: Which transform moves an element?
mcqBank.why: translate shifts position without affecting layout.

lab.brief: Replace two layout-animating properties with transform and opacity equivalents.

learn.title: Transitions need four decisions
learn.body: Transition property, duration, timing function aur delay batata hai. Sirf un properties par lagta hai jinke beech browser interpolate kar sakta hai.
learn.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Transition</title>
  <style>
    .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; transition: background-color 180ms ease, transform 180ms ease; }
    .btn:hover { background: #1d4ed8; transform: translateY(-2px); }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Hover me</button>
</body>
</html>
learn.output: Button darkens and lifts 2px over 180ms on hover; it does not jump.

learn.title: Transform moves without reflow
learn.body: translate, rotate, scale aur skew element ko paint stage par badalte hain, isliye aas-paas ka layout nahi hilta. Multiple functions ek hi transform me likho.
learn.code: Lift on hover
learn.output: Card rises 4px and scales up 1% smoothly; the surrounding layout stays in place.

learn.title: Transform origin and 3D
learn.body: transform-origin rotation ka centre badalta hai. perspective aur rotateX/rotateY depth ka illusion dete hain, lekin overuse motion sickness bhi de sakta hai.

learn.output: Badge rotates slightly anticlockwise from its left edge and grows 5% on hover.

interview.q: Which properties are cheap to animate?
interview.answer: transform and opacity, because they can be handled on the compositor without layout or paint. Animating width, top or box-shadow forces more work each frame.

interview.q: What does transform do to layout?
interview.answer: Nothing. It changes the visual rendering after layout, so neighbours do not move and the original space is preserved.

debug.title: A transition on display none
debug.code:
<style>
  .panel { display: none; transition: opacity 200ms ease; }
  .panel.open { display: block; opacity: 1; }
</style>
debug.error: display is not interpolable: the element jumps from no box to a box, so there are no intermediate frames to transition.
debug.fix:
<style>
  .panel { opacity: 0; visibility: hidden; transition: opacity 200ms ease, visibility 200ms; }
  .panel.open { opacity: 1; visibility: visible; }
</style>
debug.expected: Panel fades in over 200ms.

modules.goal: Write keyframe animations, control their timing and provide a reduced-motion path.

topics.title: Keyframes and the animation shorthand
topics.body: @keyframes named steps define karta hai; animation property name, duration, easing, delay, iteration aur direction leti hai. Shorthand order careful rakho.
topics.code: Fades up once
topics.output: Card starts 8px lower and transparent, then fades into place over 400ms and stays there.

topics.title: Iteration, direction and fill mode
topics.body: infinite repeat karta hai, alternate direction palat deta hai, aur fill mode animation ke baad ki state hold karta hai. Loader aur pulse isi se bante hain.
topics.output: A green dot that gently shrinks and fades to half opacity, then returns, forever.

topics.title: Reduced motion and performance
topics.body: prefers-reduced-motion query essential motion ko kam ya band karta hai. Sirf transform aur opacity animate karo taaki layout aur paint ka kaam kam ho.
topics.code: Floating chip

debug.title: A keyframes name that never matches
debug.broken:
<style>
  @keyframes fadeUp { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
  .card { animation: fade-up 400ms ease both; }
</style>
debug.fix:
<style>
  @keyframes fade-up { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
  .card { animation: fade-up 400ms ease both; }
</style>
debug.error: Name mismatch: keyframe names are case-sensitive and must match exactly, so no animation is attached.
debug.fixedOutput: Card fades in once over 400ms.

debug.title: An animation that snaps back at the end
debug.broken:
<style>
  @keyframes lift { to { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); } }
  .toast { animation: lift 300ms ease; }
</style>
debug.fix:
<style>
  @keyframes lift { to { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(-8px); } }
  .toast { animation: lift 300ms ease forwards; }
</style>
debug.error: No fill mode: after the animation ends the element returns to its base style, so the toast flashes back into view.
debug.fixedOutput: Toast stays faded and lifted after the animation.

tasks.title: A reduced-motion-safe pulse
tasks.statement: Build a status dot that pulses with transform and opacity, and stops when reduced motion is requested.
tasks.expected: A green dot pulsing gently; it becomes a static dot with reduced motion.

interviewBank.q: Animation or transition — which do you use?
interviewBank.answer: A transition interpolates between two states and needs a state change. An animation runs named keyframes with its own timing and can loop, so multi-step or repeating motion uses @keyframes.

interviewBank.q: Why can infinite animations hurt?
interviewBank.answer: They keep the compositor and sometimes the main thread busy, drain battery, and distract or nauseate users. Use them for short, meaningful states and respect reduced motion.

defenseBank.q: A learner copies a spinner with 20 keyframe steps.
defenseBank.answer: A few keyframes with transform are enough and cheaper. More steps only make sense for a specific visual path.

defenseBank.q: Why guard an animation with reduced motion?
defenseBank.answer: The user has told the system that motion makes them unwell. Ignoring it is an accessibility failure, not a style preference.

mcqBank.q: Which at-rule defines animation steps?
mcqBank.why: Keyframes hold the animation poses.

mcqBank.q: Which value makes an animation repeat forever?
mcqBank.why: animation-iteration-count: infinite repeats indefinitely.

modules.title: Advanced CSS and Modern Features
modules.goal: Understand the cascade, layers and specificity, and use modern layout and effects with progressive enhancement.

topics.title: Cascade, specificity and layers
topics.body: Cascade importance, origin, layer, specificity aur source order se resolve hota hai. @layer se aap poori stylesheet ki priority explicitly set kar sakte ho.
topics.code:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>Layers</title>
  <style>
    @layer base, components;
    @layer components { .btn { background: #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 10px 16px; } }
    @layer base { .btn { background: #e2e8f0; color: #0f172a; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="btn" type="button">Layered</button>
</body>
</html>
topics.output: Blue button: components is declared after base in the layer order, so its rule wins despite both matching equally.

topics.title: Feature queries, container queries and nesting
topics.body: @supports ek feature ke support par styles lagata hai, @container parent ki width par, aur nesting selectors ko ek doosre ke andar likhne deta hai.
topics.code:

Type grows with the card.
topics.output: Card content stacked with an 8px gap; the heading grows when the card itself is at least 320px wide.

topics.title: Modern effects with honest support
topics.body: aspect-ratio, object-fit, clip-path aur filters aaj widely supported hain; backdrop-filter aur some blend modes ko fallback chahiye. Feature ke saath support note karo.
topics.output: A 16:9 thumbnail that crops instead of stretching, and a circular avatar cropped to a square.

interviewBank.q: How do cascade layers change specificity?
interviewBank.answer: They do not. Layers are compared before specificity: a rule in a higher-priority layer beats a more specific rule in a lower one. Specificity only decides inside the same layer.

interviewBank.q: When do you use @supports?
interviewBank.answer: When a layout or effect has a genuine fallback, such as grid instead of floats or backdrop-filter instead of a solid surface. It should guard the enhancement, not the base experience.

defenseBank.q: A learner adds !important instead of fixing layers.
defenseBank.answer: Important reverses the layer order and makes future overrides harder. Defining layer order explicitly solves the conflict at the source.

defenseBank.q: Why not use backdrop-filter everywhere?
defenseBank.answer: It needs support and can be expensive, especially with large blurred areas. A solid or semi-transparent fallback keeps the UI legible where it is unavailable.

mcqBank.q: Which at-rule declares cascade layer order?
mcqBank.why: @layer declares and orders layers.

mcqBank.q: Which property crops an image to its box?
mcqBank.why: object-fit controls how the image fills its box.

interviewBank.q: Why keep native form controls when custom styling exists?
interviewBank.answer: Native controls bring keyboard behaviour, platform conventions and assistive-technology support. Replacing them means rebuilding all of that, usually incompletely.

interviewBank.q: What is the difference between :invalid and :user-invalid?
interviewBank.answer: :invalid matches immediately, including an empty required field on first render. :user-invalid waits until the user has interacted and the value is still invalid, which avoids a form that is red before typing.

defenseBank.q: A designer wants placeholders instead of labels.
defenseBank.answer: A placeholder disappears on typing and is not a reliable label. Keep a persistent visible label and use the placeholder only for an example.

defenseBank.q: Why not style a div as a checkbox?
defenseBank.answer: It loses keyboard toggling, focus and the checked state exposed to assistive technology. A native input with accent-color is both accessible and styleable enough.

mcqBank.q: Which property tints a native checkbox?
mcqBank.why: accent-color sets the native control accent.

mcqBank.q: Which attribute ties a label to an input?
mcqBank.why: for must match the input id.

interviewBank.q: What problem does BEM solve?
interviewBank.answer: It makes class names predictable and collision-resistant by encoding block, element and modifier, so a team can read markup and know which stylesheet owns it.

interviewBank.q: Reset or normalize?
interviewBank.answer: A reset removes defaults so every element starts from zero; normalize preserves useful defaults while fixing browser differences. Most modern projects use a small targeted reset plus tokens.

defenseBank.q: A learner wants a utility class for every property.
defenseBank.answer: Utilities explode in number and hide intent in markup. Component classes keep the design decisions in CSS; utilities are best for spacing and layout exceptions.

defenseBank.q: Why scope resets?
defenseBank.answer: A global list-style:none removes meaning from content lists. Resets should target the components that need them, not every element of a type.
steps: Show a content list without markers.

mcqBank.why: Double underscore connects an element to its block.

<!DOCTYPE html>

tasks.title: An accessibility and performance pass
tasks.statement: Fix a CTA that has low contrast, no focus ring and a width animation. Use a darker background and a transform-based transition.
tasks.solution:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <title>CTA</title>
  <style>
    .cta { background: #1d4ed8; color: #fff; padding: 12px 18px; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; transition: transform 160ms ease; }
    .cta:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); }
    .cta:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .cta { transition: none; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <button class="cta" type="button">Get started</button>
</body>
</html>
tasks.expected: High-contrast blue button, visible keyboard ring, a 1px lift on hover and no motion when reduced motion is requested.

interviewBank.q: How do you debug “my CSS is not applying”?
interviewBank.answer: Check the network entry and the selector match first, then the Styles panel for a winning rule, then specificity and source order. I change one variable at a time.

interviewBank.q: What causes layout thrash and how do you avoid it?
interviewBank.answer: Reading layout properties and then writing styles repeatedly forces synchronous reflow. Batch reads, batch writes, and animate transform and opacity instead of geometry.

defenseBank.q: A learner adds more CSS to fight a bug.
defenseBank.answer: Adding rules increases the chance of another conflict. I find which rule is winning and fix that rule instead of layering another one on top.

defenseBank.q: Why include accessibility in a debugging checklist?
defenseBank.answer: Contrast, focus and reduced motion break for real users and are cheap to catch before release. They are functional requirements, not polish.

mcqBank.q: Which DevTools panel shows the final value of a property?
mcqBank.why: The Computed panel shows resolved values after the cascade.

mcqBank.q: Which animation is cheapest for the browser?
mcqBank.why: transform can run on the compositor without layout.
